# Tune idle-admit eligibility to prefill feasibility (measured 0/31 conversion)

Discovered from: LP-0MVK35UX20081BIB (lease-gate decision item) — the AC5
tuning follow-up for LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD.

## Goal (user story)

As the operator, I want the idle-admission override (`server.local_idle_admit_enabled`)
to admit only requests the local backend can prefill to first byte inside
`local_prefill_deadline_seconds` / the ETA-guard queue budget, so the override
no longer spends GPU time on doomed prefills with zero served responses.

## Measured evidence (window 2026-10-22 21:48:05 → 2026-10-23 21:48:05)

31 `routing_idle_admit` events, **0 conversions** (0/31 local first bytes):

- 22 dispatched to a local slot and cancelled at `prefill_deadline_exceeded`
  (90 s deadline in force at the time; `lease_extended_during_prefill ...
  progress=None alive=False in_flight=True` → no observable prefill progress
  before the deadline), then detoured remote.
- 9 rejected on arrival by the ETA admission guard
  (`local_admission_guard decision=reject reason=eta_exceeds_budget_direct`,
  projected prefill 63–362 s vs the 60 s contention-queue budget).
- 0 refused by the `local_lease_active` gate; 0 first bytes.

Admitted prompt sizes 39–119 K cold tokens; window-wide `prefill_deadline_exceeded`
totalled 482 (= ~90 s per slot per abort). The after window was ~2× busier than
the before window (large_context_bypass 1,790 → 3,702; remote fallbacks 6,953 →
12,888), so this is a heavy-load measurement; the mechanism (admit → ETA-refuse
or deadline-abort) is load-independent.

Machine artifact: `docs/dev/idle-window-measurement-2026-10-22-to-2026-10-23.json`.

## Scope (candidate mechanisms to evaluate with the evidence)

- Prompt-size / projected-prefill eligibility **at admit time**: refuse the
  idle admit (keep the economic remote fallback) when `evaluate_admission`
  prices projected prefill beyond the deadline or the ETA guard would reject —
  i.e. make the override's admitted verdict consistent with the guard's
  (LP-0MVN4LBZ500281Z7 AC3c already consults the guard; measure whether the
  dispatched-and-cancelled residue remains because the guard's calibrated
  refusal and the deadline disagree).
- Priority gating: only admit below a `high`-priority tier if interactive
  latency risk is unacceptable.
- Only if the 0-conversion persists after eligibility: reconsider the
  prefill-aware idle clock (option 5 of LP-0MVK16GME007EYUW) — the measured
  window had **zero** silent-prefill refusals, so this is the fallback, not
  the primary fix.
- Explicitly NOT in scope: preempting foreign dispatch leases — rejected in
  LP-0MVK35UX20081BIB (option 1 decision); do not reopen without new evidence.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The override's admit decision is priced against projected prefill
   feasibility (ETA-guard budget + prefill deadline) and the measured
   0/31-conversion outcome is used as the regression signal: after the change,
   an equivalent window must show idle-admitted dispatches either converting
   to a first byte or being refused **before** dispatch (no
   `prefill_deadline_exceeded` on an idle-admitted session).
2. The fix is fail-safe: it can only refuse admissions the current code
   admits — it can never admit a request the guard or deadline refuses today.
3. Any new knob is config-read at dispatch time / hot-reloadable
   (`POST /admin/reload-config`), default preserves today's behaviour until
   the tuning demonstrates improvement (LP-0MVDT94F0003VHUA AC4).
4. Unit tests cover: admit-eligibility refusal on projected prefill beyond
   the deadline; the unchanged `context_too_large` cap; a calibrated vs
   uncalibrated (fail-open) bucket; and that the lease gate is untouched.
5. Docs: `docs/dev/idle-window-measurements.md`, `proxy/config.yaml` knob
   comments and `proxy/README.md` updated; decision on the flag recorded on
   LP-0MVJXGSEG0045IAF (window outcome was `measure`/`tune`, not
   `enable_by_default`).

## Related work

- LP-0MVK35UX20081BIB — parent decision (option 1: lease gate unchanged).
- LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD — parent measurement (window AC1–AC4 of record).
- LP-0MVNBJYE3003MF6J — ETA-guard and prefill-deadline interaction review
  (budget/deadline re-derivation).
- LP-0MVO8H7VQ003B12I — residual deadline evictions with zero prefill progress.
- LP-0MVN4LBZ500281Z7 / LP-0MVKUKEU80022C3U — guard/deadline bounds the
  override already consults.
data.title: Idle-admit eligibility must match prefill feasibility (measured 0/31 conversion)

data.description:
# Goal

Make the 05:00 nightly proxy usage report publish the two capacity-signal
metrics — the `slots_stale` (stale-poll) rate and the `capacity_hint`
distribution including `saturated`-without-live-work — so every night can be
compared directly against the "< 5 % stale" and "saturated only with live
work" targets without a separate standalone tool run and hand cross-check.

## Problem statement

`scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py` derives `slots_stale` rate,
`capacity_hint` distribution and saturated-without-live-work counts for an
arbitrary window, but the canonical nightly report
(`.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/`, cron at 05:00) emits neither. The post-fix
night window (2026-10-24 20:00 → 2026-10-25 07:00) therefore had to be measured
with the standalone tool and reconciled against `report.md` by hand — only
`Local attempts` (206/206) and the restart timeline could be cross-checked, so
the capacity figures had no nightly counterpart. Every future night carries the
same gap, and the two AC1 re-measurements queued after it
(LP-0MVRZDC3Y005JHQJ, LP-0MVSTQT8V002SPRZ) would each need another ad-hoc run.

## Users

- **Operator reading the 05:00 report** — "as the operator, I want tonight's
  `report.md` to show the stale-poll rate against its target, so I can judge
  the polling-path health without running another tool."
- **Producer/auditor judging AC1** — "as the producer, I want the nightly
  report to carry the same figures the acceptance criteria are written
  against, so a claim in a work item can be checked against the report of the
  matching night."
- **Follow-on measurement items** — "as the agent implementing
  LP-0MVSTQT8V002SPRZ, I want the nightly generator to emit these sections so
  the 24 h re-measurement is corroborated by the standard surface, not only by
  the standalone tool."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (stale rate section).** The nightly report renders a `slots_stale`
  section for its own window: status-poll count, polls with
  `slots_stale=true`, the rate, and the explicit outcome against a
  **configurable** stale-rate target (default < 5.0 % of polls). Polls
  without the `slots_stale` field (schema 1) are excluded from the
  denominator, never counted as fresh — the same derivation as
  `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py`. The same figures are exposed as
  an additive `--json` key, and the section is omitted (no zero-fill) when the
  window has no status polls.
- **AC2 (capacity_hint distribution).** The nightly report renders the
  `capacity_hint` distribution — `idle` / `prefill_bound` / `saturated` counts
  **and shares** of status polls, including any unexpected token rather than
  dropping it — plus the `saturated`-without-live-work count (and its share of
  polls and of `saturated` polls), using the reference live-work derivation:
  `local_in_flight_requests > 0` for schema 3, with
  `local_active_query` / `active_query` as the schema-2 fallback. Exposed as
  an additive `--json` key.
- **AC3 (reproduction of the measured window).** Re-running the analyzer with
  `--start '2026-10-24 20:00:00' --end '2026-10-25 07:00:00'` reproduces the
  recorded figures in
  `~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-10-24_post-fix-night-measurement/measurement.json`
  — 11,654 status polls; 9,278 stale (79.61 %); `idle` 4,577, `prefill_bound`
  6,024, `saturated` 1,053; 247 saturated-without-live-work — or every
  difference is explained in the work item (boundary semantics included; see
  Constraints). Verified as a test against the recorded artifact, not as a
  one-off manual run.
- **AC4 (tests).** New behaviour is covered by tests in
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/`: parser tests (synthetic
  `status_request` lines for schema 1/2/3, stale and fresh, with and without
  `local_in_flight_requests`) and rendering tests (section omitted on an empty
  window; counts, shares and target outcome asserted on a synthetic window;
  `--json` keys asserted). Tests pin the agreement with the reference
  derivation so the two surfaces cannot silently diverge. The full project
  test suite passes.
- **AC5 (documentation).** `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/SKILL.md` and
  `REFERENCE.md` describe the new section and the additive `--json` keys, the
  target and how to override it, and the schema-2/3 live-work derivation —
  consistent with the `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py` docstring it
  derives from.
- **AC6 (verification).** The nightly pipeline is run once over a closed
  window and the resulting `report.md` shows the new sections with figures that
  match the standalone tool for that window (recorded in the work item).

## Constraints

- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/**` is **agent infrastructure**: editing it
  requires explicit operator authorisation for this work item (see open
  question Q1). The intake session itself writes nothing there.
- **Single implementation of the derivation.** Do not duplicate the reference
  tool's per-line field extraction, live-work derivation or stale-rate
  denominator: extract/reuse it so both surfaces agree by construction (AC3),
  with a test that fails if they diverge.
- **Window semantics must not drift.** The analyzer currently aggregates
  events with `window_start <= ts <= window_end` (closed interval), while the
  reference tool uses `[since, until)` (half-open). The status-poll
  aggregation must adopt the reference half-open semantics (or the difference
  must be explicitly reconciled) so AC3 can match exactly.
- **The nightly run stays unattended.** No new network call, LLM call or
  interactive prompt; a window with no status polls must render a clean
  report, not fail the cron run.
- **Additive surface only.** Existing report sections, CSV artifacts and
  `--json` keys keep their meaning; nothing already published is renamed or
  changed in place. CHANGELOG.md is out of scope (ship skill owns it).
- **Scope creep guard:** attribution of stale polls by cache source/latency
  band and abandonment-event attribution are *not* in scope here; if they are
  wanted nightly, file a follow-on item rather than widening this one.

## Existing state

- Reference tool: `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py` (LP-0MVOG6YRA000T9PK,
  completed). Pure helpers to reuse: `is_status_poll()`,
  `_status_fields()` (`capacity_hint|slots_stale|slots_detail_stale|
  available_slots|local_active_query|active_query|local_in_flight_requests|
  status_schema_version|latency_ms`), `has_live_local_work()`,
  `_latency_band()`, and the `evaluate()` target checks
  (`--stale-rate-target`, default 0.05; violations target 0).
- Nightly analyzer parses `status_request` lines already
  (`log_parser.LogEvent(status_request)` with `capacity_hint`,
  `status_schema_version`, `available_slots`, `total_slots`,
  `prefill_eta_seconds`) and stores them as
  `AnalysisResult.status_request_events`, but it does **not** parse
  `slots_stale` / `slots_detail_stale`, `local_in_flight_requests`,
  `local_active_query` / `active_query` or `latency_ms`, and nothing computes
  a stale rate or a violation count.
- `reporting.py::_append_contention_prediction_section()` already prints a
  **count-only** `capacity_hint` line ("Payload's own claim (`capacity_hint`
  over status polls) ...") inside M1, and `--json` carries
  `denial_attribution.capacity_hint` plus top-level `status_capacity_hint` —
  counts only, no shares, no violations, no stale rate.
- Recorded artifact for AC3 exists and is covered:
  `~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-10-24_post-fix-night-measurement/measurement.json`
  (`coverage.covered = true`, `window_end_gap_seconds = 2.0`) with the figures
  quoted in AC3; the tool re-verified them during the 2026-10-29 audit in ~9 s.
- The proxy emits the needed fields at schema 3
  (`proxy/proxy/handlers.py`, `status_extra`: `slots_stale`,
  `slots_detail_stale`, `local_in_flight_requests`, `local_active_query`,
  `active_query`, `latency_ms`, `capacity_hint`, `status_schema_version`).
- Skill scripts are self-contained today (only their own directory on
  `sys.path`), but repo-level shared helpers are the established pattern
  (`scripts/lib/proxy_logs.py`), and the skill's tests already load repo
  `scripts/` modules by file path with a documented `sys.path` dance
  (`tests/test_admission_rate_bucket_report.py`). The 05:00 cron runs from the
  repo root, so a repo-level shared module is reachable.

## Desired change

1. One shared implementation of the status-poll derivations, imported by both
   `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py` and the nightly analyzer, so the
   numbers agree by construction (placement: open question Q2).
2. A new nightly report section (`## Local capacity signals`, rendered after
   the contention-prediction section) with: poll count; stale count/rate and
   target outcome; the `capacity_hint` counts/shares; the
   saturated-without-live-work count and shares; and a one-line verdict that
   names each unmet target instead of burying it.
3. Additive `--json` keys (e.g. `capacity_signals.slots_stale`,
   `.capacity_hint`, `.saturated_without_live_work`, `.targets`) mirroring the
   section, so automation can read what the Markdown shows.
4. A configurable stale-rate target (mechanism: open question Q3) with the
   reference tool's 0.05 default.
5. Tests for parser + aggregation + rendering + JSON + agreement with the
   reference derivation, and a reproduction test for AC3's window.

Verification commands (copy-paste, run from the repo root):

```bash
# AC3 — the nightly analyzer over the recorded post-fix night window
python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py \
    --log-dir /var/log/llama-proxy \
    --start '2026-10-24 20:00:00' --end '2026-10-25 07:00:00' \
    --output-dir /tmp/capacity-signals-check

# the reference figures for that window (already recorded)
python3 scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py \
    --since '2026-10-24 20:00' --until '2026-10-25 07:00' --window-closed \
    --label post-fix-night --json
```

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py` — parse
  `slots_stale`, `slots_detail_stale`, `local_in_flight_requests`,
  `local_active_query` / `active_query`, `latency_ms` on `status_request`
  events (additive `LogEvent` fields, `None` on pre-change lines).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/aggregation.py` — status-poll
  aggregation (counts, half-open window filter, hint histogram, violations)
  feeding the new section/JSON.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/reporting.py` — new
  `## Local capacity signals` section + additive JSON keys.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py` — stale-rate
  target option (if Q3 chooses a flag).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/` — new `test_capacity_signals.py`
  (parser/aggregation/render/JSON/agreement/reproduction).
- `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py` and `scripts/lib/` — reference
  implementation; may host or import the shared derivation (Q2).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/SKILL.md`, `REFERENCE.md` — document the
  section, keys and target.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the operator authorises edits under
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/**` for this item (Q1). Without it the item
  cannot be implemented as specified.
- **Assumption:** the section belongs in the standard report rather than a new
  artifact, and is rendered after the contention-prediction section; both are
  additive and reversible, and no existing section parser keys off section
  order (checked: only `tests/test_contention_prediction.py` splits on its own
  heading).
- **Risk (window boundary):** an inclusive-end analyzer window would count
  polls the reference tool excludes, breaking exact AC3 reproduction. Mitigated
  by adopting half-open semantics for status polls and by a boundary test with
  a poll at exactly `end`.
- **Risk (divergent copies):** extracting the helpers can leave a stale copy
  in either surface. Mitigated by a test that asserts both surfaces produce
  identical figures on the same synthetic lines.
- **Risk (report noise):** a 24 h window makes the stale rate easy to
  misread as capacity truthfulness. The section text must repeat the reference
  tool's caveat: the stale rate is a *polling-path* signal and is only
  meaningful with the build it was measured on.
- **Risk (unexpected vocabulary):** a future `capacity_hint` token must appear
  as its own row rather than being dropped or silently bucketed.
- **Risk (cron breakage):** a log window with no status polls (or no logs) must
  render an empty/absent section, not raise — the nightly run is unattended.
- **Risk (silent truncation):** unlike the reference tool, the nightly analyzer
  has no coverage-gap verdict, so a window whose retained logs are incomplete
  would publish a plausible-but-partial rate. The AC3 comparison must record
  that the reference run reported `coverage.covered = true` for the window,
  and the section must state when the poll count is derived from logs that do
  not span the whole window (or the limitation must be documented).

## Related work

- **LP-0MVOG6YRA000T9PK** (completed) — the standalone verification tool whose
  derivations this item publishes.
- **LP-0MVLNBCTN0084MT0** (open, plan_complete) — parent measurement whose AC1
  (`slots_stale` < 5 %, `saturated` only with live work) needs a nightly
  counterpart.
- **LP-0MVOG7IX6006MZ23** (completed) — publishing work this item was
  discovered from; the hand cross-check gap.
- **LP-0MVOG7IP80003MLV** (open, plan_complete) — post-fix night measurement
  supplying the AC3 reference artifact.
- **LP-0MVRZDC3Y005JHQJ**, **LP-0MVSTQT8V002SPRZ** (open) — successor
  re-measurements that would otherwise each need another ad-hoc tool run;
  LP-0MVSTQT8V002SPRZ records AC3 as "partial: attribution complete but not in
  the nightly generator", which this item addresses for the capacity figures.
- **LP-0MVRMI5HK00558TB** (in-progress) — abandoned-dispatch/cooldown bug that
  can move the violation count; not a dependency, but it must be recorded when
  comparing night to night.
- Reference artifact:
  `~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-10-24_post-fix-night-measurement/` (`REPORT.md`,
  `measurement.json`, `measurement.txt`).

## Open questions (see Appendix)

- Q1 — authorisation to edit `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/**`.
- Q2 — where the single shared derivation lives.
- Q3 — how the stale-rate target is configured.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1: Is operator authorisation granted to edit
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/**` for this work item?**
  Options: (a) authorised for this item; (b) not authorised — keep the change
  outside the skill; (c) authorised, but the change must be reviewed by the
  producer before it is pushed to `dev`.
  **Recommended:** (a) authorised for this item — the constraint exists to
  protect agent infrastructure, and the change is additive to the report
  only; (c) is the fallback if the operator wants a review gate.
  — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** (no producer reply in this session; recorded
  2026-10-29). Context: `git log` shows the last changes to this skill
  (694ed2a5, bb4bcb3c) landed through normal implementation items, but this
  item's own constraint explicitly requires authorisation.

- **Q2: Where should the single shared derivation live so both surfaces agree
  by construction?**
  Options: (a) extract pure helpers into `scripts/lib/capacity_signals.py`;
  the standalone tool imports it natively, the skill loads it through a small
  documented path-based shim (precedent:
  `tests/test_admission_rate_bucket_report.py`); (b) the analyzer shells out to
  `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py --json`; (c) implement inside the
  skill and have the standalone tool import the skill module; (d) two
  implementations plus a cross-check test.
  **Recommended:** (a) — one implementation, repo convention for shared
  helpers (`scripts/lib/proxy_logs.py`), no subprocess or coverage-model
  coupling, and the cron already runs from the repo root.
  — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** (recorded 2026-10-29).

- **Q3: How should the stale-rate target be configured?**
  Options: (a) a new `--stale-rate-target` flag on `analyze_proxy_usage.py`,
  default 0.05, mirroring the reference tool; (b) a key in
  `proxy/config.yaml` read through `config_loader`; (c) both (flag overrides
  config).
  **Recommended:** (a) — matches the reference tool's surface, needs no
  config-schema change, and the cron line can carry an override if the target
  ever moves.
  — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** (recorded 2026-10-29).

## Headline

The 05:00 nightly report gains a `slots_stale` rate (against a configurable
< 5 % target) and a full `capacity_hint` distribution including
`saturated`-without-live-work, derived from one shared implementation with
`scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py` and verified by reproducing the
recorded 2026-10-24 post-fix night figures (11,654 polls / 79.61 % / 247
violations).
data.title: Nightly proxy usage report: publish slots_stale rate and capacity_hint distribution

data.description:
# Intake Brief — Abandoned local dispatches leave llama-server busy and start a 600 s prefill_thrash_cooldown

## Problem statement

332 local dispatches were abandoned in the measured 11 h window but llama-server
kept computing them, so fresh `/slots` polls reported `capacity_hint=saturated`
with `local_in_flight_requests=0` for work nobody was waiting for (247 polls,
2.12 %). The same abandonments each arm the per-session 600 s
`prefill_thrash_cooldown`, which then skipped local routing 916 times in that
window — including 241 skips for 21 `herdr-*` sessions and 336 skips while the
GPU was demonstrably free — the leading explanation for the night reaching 5
herdr downtime dispatches against the ≥ 10 target.

## Users / stakeholders

- **Operator**: *"As the operator, I want an abandoned local dispatch to stop
  consuming the GPU, so a new dispatch is not admitted into a ghost's shadow and
  my capacity reading (`saturated`) means live work."*
- **herdr downtime dispatcher**: *"As the downtime dispatcher, I want a cooldown
  armed by one doomed prompt not to veto my next dispatch — a different, usually
  smaller prompt on an idle GPU — for the next 10 minutes, so I reach ≥ 10
  dispatches a night."*
- **Proxy maintainer**: *"As a maintainer I want the abandonment → capacity-signal
  → routing chain to be attributable from log lines alone, so a regression in
  either direction (ghost saturation, or a cooldown that starves routing) is
  caught by measurement rather than by night-time dispatch counts."*

## Measured evidence

### From the published measurement (LP-0MVOG7IP80003MLV, `measurement.json`)

Window 2026-10-24 20:00 → 2026-10-25 07:00 local (Europe/Dublin), 11 h,
11 654 status polls:

| abandonment reason | events |
|---|---|
| `prefill_deadline` | 260 |
| `session_evicted` | 60 |
| `no_progress_watchdog` | 11 |
| `client_disconnect` | 1 |
| **total** | **332** |

- `saturated` with `local_in_flight_requests=0` **and** `slots_detail_stale=false`:
  **247 polls** (2.12 % of polls, 23.46 % of the 1 053 `saturated` polls).
- 100 % attributed within the 600 s lookback: 204 `prefill_deadline`,
  43 `session_evicted`, 0 unattributed
  (`saturated_without_live_work_attribution.csv`).
- The reconciliation rules of LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM held: **zero** stale-detail
  poll claimed `saturated` without live work. This is therefore *not* a
  capacity-signal correctness defect — it is abandoned work, truthfully reported.

### Re-derived during intake (2026-10-29, same window, `/var/log/llama-proxy` proxy logs)

`routing_skip_local … reason=prefill_thrash_cooldown` in the same window:

- **916 skips** across **46 distinct sessions**.
- **241 skips (26.3 %) for 21 distinct `herdr-*` sessions** — the downtime
  dispatcher's own workload. Worst cases: `herdr-1792881165-2418241-523`
  30 skips (23:39:17 → 23:47:47), `herdr-1792882467-2826087-398` 26 skips
  (00:00:49 → 00:04:56), `herdr-1792884313-3423920-2499` 22 skips
  (00:32:00 → 00:52:02).
- **336 skips (36.7 %)** carry a nearest preceding status poll (≤ 120 s) that
  reports `local_in_flight_requests=0`; 308 of those with
  `capacity_hint=idle`, `available_slots=2` — i.e. the proxy declined local
  routing while its own snapshot said the GPU was free.
- 135 of the 260 `prefill_deadline` abandonments belong to `herdr-*` sessions
  (170 `lease_released` events in total for `herdr-*` sessions, counting the
  reasons the tool does not classify as abandonment): the cooldown is largely
  being armed *by* the dispatcher it then starves.
- Counter-example of the opposite defect (the sibling item's evidence): session
  `01a16fa8-03e5-7600-aa7f-04e575dc9f1a` armed at 22:06:23, re-dispatched local
  at 22:07:53 and 22:09:23 with **no** `routing_skip_local` line — the gate does
  not engage on every path either, so over- and under-application coexist.

### llama-server abort behaviour (why closing the stream is not enough)

- llama-server logs **0** `client disconnected` occurrences; cancellation appears
  only as `Connection handling canceled` → `stop: cancel task` →
  `slot release: … stop processing`, i.e. at an HTTP write point
  (`llama-server.log-2026-10-28`). A mid-prefill abandonment therefore is not
  aborted early: the prefill runs to completion and only the leftover
  generation is discarded, which is exactly the ghost that later polls see.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Abandoned work stops being reported as live saturated work.** For
  every abandonment reason in {`prefill_deadline`, `session_evicted`,
  `no_progress_watchdog`, `client_disconnect`} the proxy either (a) actively
  cancels the upstream llama-server task, or (b) records the abandoned slot
  identity and exposes it distinctly in the status payload (e.g. a
  busy-but-not-ours annotation) so abandoned work is never counted as
  `saturated` *with live work*. Measured over a comparable window:
  `saturated` with `local_in_flight_requests=0` and `slots_detail_stale=false`
  ≈ 0 (baseline 247 polls / 2.12 %). The chosen mechanism per reason is
  documented, and a genuinely busy GPU is never folded into `idle`.
- **AC2 — A cooldown armed by one abandonment must not veto local routing while
  the GPU is demonstrably free.** Observable obligations: (i) a re-dispatch of
  the failing prompt is still refused (the gate's intent is preserved), and
  (ii) a request whose prompt is *not* the failing one is routed local when the
  proxy's own fresh snapshot shows the GPU free (no live dispatch,
  `local_in_flight_requests=0`, `slots_detail_stale=false`). *How* this is
  achieved — prompt-fingerprint scoping of the window, a free-GPU release, or
  both — is an implementation decision recorded in the Appendix; the AC is
  measured by behaviour, not by mechanism. Before/after measured with the same
  tool over comparable windows: baseline 916 skips (46 sessions, 241 `herdr-*`,
  336 with a free GPU); the post-fix target is zero skips with a demonstrably
  free GPU. The gate keeps engaging where it should (see Constraints) — this AC
  narrows what it vetoes, it does not disable it; rollback knob
  `server.local_prefill_thrash_cooldown_seconds: 0` still disables the window.
- **AC3 — Tests cover the new cancellation/cooldown behaviour with mocked
  llama-server responses (no live dependency).** Per-reason coverage of the
  abandonment paths, an injected clock for the cooldown lifetimes, the
  same-prompt-still-refused and different-prompt-admitted cases, the
  free-GPU release, and the rollback knob; the full suite passes.
- **AC4 — Re-measurement over one comparable night (same tool, same window
  length).** Report (a) `saturated`-without-live-work ≈ 0 and (b) herdr downtime
  dispatches within the parent's ≥ 10/night target, or document precisely why
  not (with the evidence limits, as LP-0MVOG7IP80003MLV AC3 did).
- **AC5 — Documentation updated**: `proxy/docs/routing.md` (post-deadline
  cooldown section and the abandonment/capacity interaction),
  `proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md` (status semantics for abandoned
  work), `proxy/README.md`, and the code comments at each changed path.
- **AC6 — Full project test suite passes with the new changes** (run through the
  test skill; the dev-push gate enforces the full suite).

## Constraints

- **Do not weaken the truthful-status rules of LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM**: a fresh
  snapshot that genuinely reports *live* processing must still be able to say
  `saturated`. Any "not ours" exclusion must therefore be explicit and
  attributable (slot/task identity), never a blanket discount of llama-server
  processing.
- **Do not weaken cooldown gate engagement** (LP-0MVSAMN14001DMTY /
  LP-0MVPUBQLQ008GJOV): the cooldown must still refuse a re-dispatch of the
  failing prompt on every dispatch path. This item removes over-broad scope and
  adds a release condition; it does not remove the gate.
- Do not change the prefill deadline (90 s shipped / 120 s default), the 180 s
  no-progress watchdog, or the 10 s sweep cadence.
- Re-measurement is read-only: never restart or kill the proxy to obtain
  evidence (and never a blanket `pkill`/`killall` — see project AGENTS.md).
- Do not edit `.pi/` agent infrastructure (e.g. `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/**`);
  record an Open Question instead.

## Existing state

- `proxy/proxy/router.py` — the `prefill_deadline_exceeded` branch arms
  `_record_prefill_thrash_cooldown(session_id, …, tokens=…)`, releases the
  lease/marker via `_release_prefill_deadline_dispatch`, then `client.aclose()`s
  the upstream session. No abandoned-slot identity is retained, and (see above)
  llama-server does not notice the close until it next writes.
- `proxy/proxy/server.py` — `lease_released … reason=session_evicted` releases
  every record for the session but holds no upstream stream handle, so it cannot
  cancel anything.
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — the `no_progress_watchdog` path does capture
  and cancel the upstream `stream_cm` (from LP-0MVIQ0FJC000YLX0); that mechanism
  exists but is not used by the other two reasons.
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `_prefill_thrash_cooldowns` is a
  `dict[session_id → deadline]`, armed for 600 s, cleared lazily on expiry, by a
  comparable-size successful first byte (`local_prefill_thrash_recovery_fraction`,
  LP-0MVQITN6P008DPLB) or by knob 0. It has no prompt fingerprint and no
  free-GPU release.
- `proxy/proxy/observability.py` / `capacity_admission.py` — `capacity_hint` is
  derived from the llama-server `/slots` snapshot plus
  `local_in_flight_requests`; it has no notion of "processing, but abandoned".
- `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py` — measures polls, stale rate,
  `capacity_hint`, `saturated`-without-live-work and herdr dispatches, but does
  **not** count `routing_skip_local reason=prefill_thrash_cooldown`; the before/after
  for AC2 needs it added (a small, additive metric) so the numbers stay
  re-derivable by the same tool.

## Desired change

- An abandonment must end in a *real* release of the GPU (best effort) **or** an
  attributable "busy, not ours" status, so `saturated` never covers abandoned
  work again.
- The post-deadline cooldown must suppress only the re-dispatch it was armed for
  (same prompt, same session) and a free GPU must never be skipped because of it.
- Both behaviours must be visible in log/measurement output so the repair is
  verifiable without another night of guesswork.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/router.py` — deadline branch: retain abandoned slot/task identity,
  extend the upstream cancel to this path; arm the cooldown with the prompt
  fingerprint.
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — cooldown store keying/release helpers,
  `_release_prefill_deadline_dispatch`, `_try_acquire_local_dispatch`,
  abandoned-slot registry.
- `proxy/proxy/server.py` — `session_evicted` release path (cancel what can be
  cancelled, annotate the rest).
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — the local-branch gate
  (`_prefill_thrash_cooldown_remaining`) must take the prompt fingerprint and the
  free-GPU evidence into account without losing gate engagement.
- `proxy/proxy/observability.py` — status payload / `capacity_hint` derivation for
  the "busy, not ours" annotation.
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_thrash_cooldown.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_prefill_thrash_wedge.py` — deterministic harnesses to extend
  (mocked llama-server, injected clock).
- `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py` — add the cooldown-skip metric
  (and skips-while-idle) for AC2/AC4.
- `proxy/docs/routing.md`, `proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md`,
  `proxy/README.md` — documentation.

## Risks, assumptions, failure modes

- **Assumption**: llama-server cannot abort an in-flight prefill through the
  proxy's SSE close (evidence above); a genuine abort would need an out-of-band
  signal (task/slot-level cancel), which may not exist on this build. AC1 allows
  the annotated-exclusion route precisely for that case.
- **Risk — exclusion degrades truthfulness**: reporting a busy-but-abandoned GPU
  as `idle` would admit fresh dispatches behind a ghost and make the tail worse.
  Mitigation: explicit annotation, never a silent discount.
- **Risk — cooldown becomes a no-op**: making the release condition too eager
  re-opens the prefill thrash that LP-0MVKUKFHH005UDWL fixed (41 local POSTs
  re-prefilling the same prompt). Mitigation: keep "same failing prompt is
  refused" as a hard assertion in AC3.
- **Risk — conflict with LP-0MVSAMN14001DMTY** (blocked, gate engagement at every
  entry): implementing AC2 as "skip the gate when the GPU is idle" could mask
  their fix. Mitigation: this item changes *arming scope and release*, not gate
  engagement; AC2's free-GPU release is only meaningful once AC1 removes ghosts,
  so implement AC1 first.
- **Failure mode — ghost accounting drift**: `local_active_queries`,
  `local_prefill_in_flight` and the slot registry must stay consistent with
  whatever is recorded as abandoned (the LP-0MVKUKFSO008GI6O family).
- **Risk — measurement-tool drift**: `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py`
  already produces the numbers other items and the nightly report rely on
  (LP-0MVOG6YRA000T9PK). The AC2 metric must be additive; existing metric
  definitions, names and JSON shapes must not change.
- **Scope-creep risk**: admission-side prevention (`local_cold_prefill_budget_tokens`,
  LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D) and lease fairness (LP-0MVOJ6KAW004EBV0) overlap the
  evidence; record any such work as a linked item instead of absorbing it here.

## Definition of Done

AC1–AC6 met; the AC4 re-measurement is run over one comparable night with its
artifacts saved under a named directory in `~/proxy-usage-reports/`; the AC2
before/after counts come from the same tool invocation shape; the full suite is
green.

## Related work

- **LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM** (completed) — the truthful-status contract this item must
  not weaken; its measurement child LP-0MVOG7IP80003MLV supplied the numbers.
- **LP-0MVPUBQLQ008GJOV** (open, plan_complete) — in-request local re-dispatch
  after a prefill-deadline cancellation; its children
  **LP-0MVSAMN14001DMTY** (blocked; gate engagement on every dispatch entry, lease
  cleared before retry) and **LP-0MVSAM2AV0077UAE** (deterministic regression)
  and **LP-0MVSAMS5O006OAIS** (verification/docs) share the cancellation and
  cooldown code paths. Boundary: they own *under-engagement* (a path that bypasses
  the gate, the fresh lease ~150 ms after release); this item owns *over-broad
  engagement* (session-wide 600 s veto, free-GPU skips) and the ghost capacity
  signal.
- **LP-0MVKUKFHH005UDWL** (completed) — the post-deadline cooldown itself.
- **LP-0MVQITN6P008DPLB** (completed) — recovery-fraction clearing; the mechanism
  AC2 extends.
- **LP-0MVIQ0FJC000YLX0** (completed) — precedent: cancel the upstream stream on a
  confirmed-dead dispatch (watchdog path), the mechanism to extend to the other
  abandonment reasons.
- **LP-0MVO7IDTP005S92D** (completed) — session-eviction record/lease release
  shapes (`session_evicted` is the second-largest abandonment reason here).
- **LP-0MVRZDC3Y005JHQJ**, **LP-0MVSTQT8V002SPRZ** (open) — re-measurement siblings;
  AC4 here should reuse their window tooling rather than invent a parallel path.
- **LP-0MVLNBCTN0084MT0** (open) — parent measurement item whose ≥ 10/night herdr
  dispatch target AC4 tests against.

## Appendix: clarifying questions and answers

- Q (intake, answered from evidence — no producer round trip needed): "Which
  cooldown skips actually starve routing, and how would 'the GPU is demonstrably
  free' be measured?" — Answer (intake, proxy logs, same window): 916 skips /
  46 sessions / 241 `herdr-*` / 21 herdr sessions; 336 skips (36.7 %) fall where
  the nearest ≤ 120 s status poll reports `local_in_flight_requests=0` (308 with
  `capacity_hint=idle`, `available_slots=2`). Operational definition for AC2:
  nearest fresh status poll within 120 s with `local_in_flight_requests=0` and
  `slots_detail_stale=false`. Source:
  `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log{,-2026-10-25_00,.2026-10-24_22,.2026-10-25_04}*`,
  window 2026-10-24 20:00 → 2026-10-25 07:00.
- Q (OPEN QUESTION — implementation must resolve, with recommended option):
  "AC1 offers 'cancel upstream' *or* 'exclude from the signal'. Which is
  achievable on this llama-server build?"
  — Answer: **_not yet determined_**. Evidence: llama-server logs zero
  `client disconnected` events and only cancels at an HTTP write point, so the
  proxy's `client.aclose()` on the deadline path does not abort a mid-prefill
  task; the watchdog path already cancels a captured `stream_cm` and is the only
  reason with a handle. **Recommended (advisory):** hybrid — extend the
  stream-cancel to every reason that has a handle (`prefill_deadline`), record the
  abandoned slot identity for the ones that do not (`session_evicted`,
  `client_disconnect`), and report those slots as "busy, not ours" rather than
  `saturated`; investigate an out-of-band llama-server cancel as a separate
  finding if the annotation proves insufficient.
- Q (OPEN QUESTION — implementation must resolve, with recommended option):
  "How should AC2 scope the cooldown — per prompt fingerprint, per size band, or
  release-on-free-GPU?"
  — Answer: **_not yet determined_**. A size band is too coarse (two different
  60 k prompts share a band); a bare release-on-free-GPU is circular while ghosts
  still exist, because the GPU is genuinely busy finishing the abandoned prefill.
  **Recommended (advisory):** both — key the window by (session, prompt
  fingerprint) so only the failing prompt is refused, *and* release it when a
  fresh snapshot proves the GPU free; that combination is only sound after AC1
  lands, which is why AC1 should be implemented first.
- Q (OPEN QUESTION — sequencing, with recommended option): "Does AC2 conflict with
  LP-0MVSAMN14001DMTY's 'gate engages at every local-dispatch entry'?"
  — Answer: **_no, if scoped as above_**; the sibling item fixes paths that
  *bypass* the gate, this item narrows *what the gate refuses*. Implementation
  must not weaken gate engagement, and the AC3 test matrix must assert both
  directions (same prompt refused on every path; different prompt admitted when
  free). **Recommended (advisory):** land this item's arming/release change
  without touching the sibling item's dispatch-entry coverage, and re-run the
  sibling's engagement test as a regression.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MQNZXZUH002FTON** – Implement host-first llama-server startup (llama_allow_host_fallback) (completed)
- **LP-0MNA7FYH4001ZUR4** – Router-mode llama-server integration (completed)
- **LP-0MQ1JJ9JQ004Z48P** – server: add dev mode startup with auto-reload and DEBUG logging (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — matched: 0mvkukfhh005udwl, 0mvkukfso008gi6o, abandoned, able, abort (+457 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: able, abort, ac1, ac2, ac3 (+450 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_nothink.txt` — matched: able, abort, ac1, ac2, ac3 (+450 more)

## Goal

Produce the measured evidence the AC3 closure verdict needs: a ≥24 h post-landing window of `local_eviction_after_acceptance reason=prefill_deadline` events, with the user-traffic / audit-session split and a per-event cause attribution (occupancy / capacity / predicted-warmth), so the tracking item LP-0MVO8H7VQ003B12I can decide AC3(a) versus AC3(b).

## Background — the original premise is superseded by later measurement

- The scheduler epic LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG and its occupancy-aware child LP-0MVOFVCA2008DQVE are **completed** (commit `8b7ab7a2`, in `HEAD`; the proxy restarted with it at 2026-10-26T10:23Z).
- A later measurement on LP-0MVQIT9QY007QU27 (window 2026-10-26 09:06 → 2026-10-27 09:06, 114 events) **falsified the second-slot head-of-line hypothesis**: 68 % of events overlapped no other prefill or decode, and `local_in_flight_requests` reached 2 in only 11 % of windows. 29 events (25 %) were "fake-warm": prompt ≈56 k, priced `new_tokens` 17–182, `eta_prefill_s` 3.7–13.8 s, cancelled at 120 s.
- The cause attributed there is predicted-but-unmeasured warmth: all 5 456 `routing_resident_prefix` decisions in that window carry `n_past_actual=none`. The fix is LP-0MVQIT9QY007QU27 (Option D, `measured_cache_deficit` early abort), whose F5 LP-0MVR7IXAI002QXXD owns the fix's own ≥24 h post-deploy measurement.
- **Do not repeat F5.** Consume its output where available and add only what the AC3 verdict needs (user/audit split, occupancy-vs-warmth attribution, per-reason counts).

## Scope

**In:** window and deploy-timestamp selection; log mining over `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log*`; user-traffic vs audit classification using the **same classifier** as the parent AC4 measurement (LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D); per-event attribution; a recorded dataset plus the exact commands needed to reproduce it.

**Out:** any code change (admission, deadlines, budgets, queue bounds, slot counts); the AC3 verdict itself (sibling verdict item); rewriting parent AC4. Any further admission-maths change discovered while measuring is filed as a new linked work item (`discovered-from` this item), never folded in here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Window and deploy timestamps recorded.** The ≥24 h measurement window and the deploy timestamp of every admission-affecting change inside it (at minimum `8b7ab7a2` and the Option D commit) are recorded on this item **before** measuring; any proxy restart, config reload or slot-count change inside the window is recorded as a re-base event.
- **AC2 — Parent-AC1 evidence reported.** The 22-event/7.4 h measurement (12 user-traffic) with the `progress=0` signature and the audit-load split is reported against the new window using the same classifier, so the two reports are comparable and can be referenced from the parent AC4 comment by the verdict item.
- **AC3 — Parent-AC3 counts reported.** For the window: total `reason=prefill_deadline` events, the user-traffic vs audit-session split, the hourly rate for each, and the `new_tokens` / `eta_prefill_s` / `elapsed_s` distributions — reported against both the 22-event/7.4 h baseline and the 114-event fix-item window.
- **AC4 — Cause attribution per event.** Each event is classified as **occupancy** (another session's prefill or lease in flight in the same slot pool), **capacity** (slot saturation with no other occupant) or **predicted-warmth** (large prompt, tiny priced `new_tokens`, actual prefill progress far above the priced compute), with the classification rules and evidence columns recorded. The occupancy share is the direct test of this item's original hypothesis.
- **AC5 — Conversion accounted.** `reason=measured_cache_deficit` (Option D) is reported alongside `prefill_deadline`, so a fall in one reason is never misread as the residual disappearing.
- **AC6 — Parent AC3 mapping (evidence half).** "**AC3 — Closure.** Closed only when either (a) the scheduler epic lands and a post-landing window shows zero user-traffic `prefill_deadline` evictions after acceptance, or (b) the producer explicitly re-scopes parent AC4 with an agreed threshold and the re-scoped criterion is met." — this item supplies the measured evidence for path (a) and, when (a) fails, the evidence for the (b) re-scope proposal; it does not close the tracking item.

## Key Files

- `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log*` (window evidence)
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py` (existing analysis flow)
- `proxy/proxy/admission_events.py` (`log_local_eviction`, `EVICTION_REASONS` — the closed reason vocabulary)

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption — the post-fix window is a valid evidence window.** It is only valid if the deploy timestamps are recorded first and no admission-affecting change or slot-count change occurs inside it (AC1 re-bases the window otherwise).
- **Risk — attribution drift.** The user-traffic / audit classifier must be the parent AC4 one, or the two reports stop being comparable (AC2).
- **Risk — misreading the reason conversion.** A fall in `reason=prefill_deadline` with a rise in `reason=measured_cache_deficit` is Option D doing its job, not the residual disappearing (AC5).
- **Reuse:** LP-0MVR7IXAI002QXXD (F5) already measures the fix's own post-deploy window; this item consumes that output rather than duplicating it.

## Deliverables

A recorded window analysis (dataset + reproducible commands) posted as a comment on this item, with the attribution table and explicit pointers for the AC3(a) / AC3(b) verdict.

# Investigate: dev-push full-suite gate can validate the wrong tree on the non-fast-forward retry path

## Problem statement

The dev-push full-suite gate in `.githooks/pre-push` runs
`run_tests.py --scope full --project-root "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"`,
i.e. it verifies the tree of the **directory the push was launched from**, not
the tree of the commit actually being pushed. `implement.py finish` normally
makes those coincide by fast-forwarding the main checkout to the new commit
before pushing from the main checkout — but the non-fast-forward retry path
breaks that invariant: `_recover_non_fast_forward_push()` rebases inside the
worktree (rewriting the commit) and retries
`git_push_to_dev(repo_root, …)` from the **main checkout**, which is still at
the pre-rebase commit. The gate therefore verifies an unrelated commit's tree
while the rebased commit lands on `dev` ungated.

## Users

- **AI agents running `/skill:implement`** — the dev-push gate is the only
  full-suite enforcement point for `dev`/`main` pushes; they rely on "the push
  succeeded" meaning "the full suite ran against what landed".
- **Producers / release operators** — rely on the invariant *landed on `dev`
  ⇒ full suite green at that commit* when approving a finish or a release.
- **Audit / reviewers** — rely on the cached full-suite entry at the pushed
  commit as the evidence trail (`run_tests.py --summary`, audit F3).

Example user stories:

- "As an agent finishing a work item, when `dev` has advanced and my push is
  rebased and retried, I expect the suite to have run against the rebased
  commit — not against whatever the main checkout happens to contain."
- "As a producer, when a commit lands on `dev` I expect to be able to prove
  which tree the gate verified."

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Gate subject is the pushed commit.** For a push whose target is
   `refs/heads/dev` or `refs/heads/main`, the gate runs the full suite against
   the pushed commit's tree (git state: pushed SHA, clean). A mismatch between
   the push cwd's `HEAD` and the pushed `local_sha` must never silently verify
   the wrong tree: it must either be gated correctly or refused with an
   actionable message.
2. **Retry path explicitly covered.** The non-fast-forward retry path (rebase
   rewrites the commit, push retried from the main checkout) is handled
   explicitly, and the post-rebase commit is the tree under test.
3. **Gate evidence is observable.** Every gate run records the resolved tree
   (root path, `HEAD` sha, pushed sha) and the outcome (executed vs cache hit),
   and the push path surfaces that evidence (at least INFO/DEBUG) so "the gate
   ran and hit a cache for commit X" is distinguishable from "the gate never
   ran".
4. **Regression test for the retry path.** An automated test asserts which
   tree the gate verifies on the retry path (and on a `HEAD` ≠ pushed-sha
   mismatch) — no reliance on wall-clock timing as a proxy.
5. **No fail-open.** The gate must not become satisfiable by an unrelated
   cache entry, and the documented bypasses (`TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1`) must remain
   explicit, non-default escape hatches.
6. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes**, including
   code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (at
   minimum `docs/dev/git-hooks.md`: state that the gate's subject is the
   pushed commit and how its evidence is surfaced).
7. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Repository boundary.** `implement.py` is a framework file owned by
  SorraAgents (`~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`,
  installed into `~/.pi/agent/skills`); this repository owns
  `.githooks/pre-push`, `tests/test_git_hooks.py` and `docs/dev/git-hooks.md`
  and ships no `skill/` tree. Worktree isolation means a `LP` worktree cannot
  edit the framework copy. *(See OPEN QUESTION Q1 — this decides where the
  fix lands.)*
- **Cache compatibility.** The audit's accepted full-suite evidence is the
  cache entry keyed by *suite command + git state* (`HEAD` sha + content hash
  of dirty paths, see `skill/test_cache.py::compute_git_state`). Keys are
  **path-independent**, so verifying the same commit from a different
  directory still reuses an existing entry — any fix must preserve that
  property and keep writing audit-acceptable entries (`scope: full`).
- **Cost.** A correct gate must not turn every `dev` push into a cold
  ~6 min run when a valid entry exists for the pushed commit; conversely it
  must not accept an entry for a different commit.
- **No weakening of other gates.** Branch policy, context-budget gate,
  worklog sync and `mirror_suite_cache` behaviour must keep working from both
  the main checkout and linked worktrees.
- **Scope discipline.** Fixing the *general* "gate verifies the pushed commit"
  gap is in scope; hunting the 2026-10-28 timing anomaly beyond instrumentation
  is not (see Risks).

## Existing state

- `.githooks/pre-push` — the full-suite gate resolves
  `repo_root="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"` from the **push cwd**, passes
  it as `--project-root`, and logs a generic "full-suite gate … running"
  line. It never compares `repo_root`'s `HEAD` with the pushed `local_sha`
  read from stdin. `mirror_suite_cache` already mirrors gate entries from a
  worktree's private cache into the main checkout's `.worklog/cache`.
- `implement.py finish` — Step 5 fast-forwards the main checkout's `dev` to
  the new commit; Step 6 pushes from `repo_root` (main checkout,
  `implement.py:5235`); on `PushNonFastForwardError` it calls
  `_recover_non_fast_forward_push()`, which fetches, rebases **in the
  worktree**, then retries `git_push_to_dev(repo_root, …)`
  (`implement.py:4737`). Nothing re-points the main checkout at the rebased
  commit afterwards (`_sync_parent_branch` runs only after a successful push
  and fast-forwards local `dev` to `origin/dev`).
- `git_push_to_dev()` captures hook output with `subprocess.PIPE` and logs
  `stderr` **only on failure**, so a successful gate run (executed or cached)
  leaves no trace in the finish log.
- Precedent: `LP-0MVFFJWPW007ZEPK` wired `core.hooksPath` (gate now active —
  `scripts/install_git_hooks.sh --check` passes); `LP-0MVHSWUE80097KQJ`
  recorded the pre-wiring period where no gate ran at all.
- Sibling defect, same root cause: **LP-0MVSJUM3O003C0H9** — the gate
  verifies a stale main checkout when the Step-5 fast-forward is *skipped*
  (dirty main checkout). This item is scoped to the gaps that item does not
  cover (retry path, gate evidence, retry-path regression test); the two
  share a fix surface.
- **Unexplained (instrumentation target).** In the observed finish
  (2026-10-28, `LP-0MVQ239VQ001RXZ0`) the whole finish — commit, failed push,
  rebase, successful push — took ~68 s, far below a cold full-suite run
  (~356–386 s), and no cache entry existed for the pushed tree. Neither
  push's hook appears to have executed the suite, which a cache hit on the
  retry alone cannot explain (git pulls the pre-push hook *before* contacting
  the remote, so the non-fast-forward rejection must come after it).

## Desired change

Shape depends on the answers to Q1/Q2; the invariant to establish is:

- the gate's subject is the **pushed commit's tree**, verified explicitly
  rather than assumed from the push cwd;
- the retry path re-establishes that subject after the rebase rewrites the
  commit;
- every gate run leaves observable evidence naming the tree it verified.

Candidate mechanisms (decided by Q1/Q2):

- **Gate-side (this repo):** the hook compares `HEAD` at the resolved root
  with the pushed `local_sha`; on mismatch it either gates the pushed commit
  (e.g. in a temporary detached worktree at `local_sha`) or fails closed with
  an actionable message, and it logs the resolved root/`HEAD`/pushed sha plus
  the cache outcome.
- **Pusher-side (SorraAgents):** the retry (and ideally the first push) runs
  from the worktree where the pushed commit is checked out, or passes the
  pushed tree explicitly; hook/push stderr is surfaced at INFO/DEBUG on
  success too.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.githooks/pre-push` — assert/gate the pushed commit's tree; emit gate
  evidence (resolved root, `HEAD`, pushed sha, executed vs cached).
- `tests/test_git_hooks.py` — regression tests: `HEAD` ≠ pushed sha (retry
  path simulation) is gated correctly or refused; gate evidence is emitted;
  existing gate tests keep passing.
- `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` — document the gate's subject and its evidence.
- *(only if Q1 includes the framework half)*
  `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — retry push
  from the worktree / explicit pushed tree, stderr surfaced on success;
  `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/implement/tests/` — retry-path regression
  test around `_recover_non_fast_forward_push` / `git_push_to_dev`.

## Related work

- **LP-0MVSJUM3O003C0H9** — dev-push full-suite gate verifies a stale main
  checkout when the pre-push fast-forward is skipped (open). Same root cause,
  different trigger; partial overlap — this item covers the retry path, gate
  evidence and the retry-path regression test. Whichever lands first should
  be reviewed against the other's ACs.
- **LP-0MVQ239VQ001RXZ0** — origin of this investigation (the finish whose
  retry landed ungated); discovered-from link.
- **LP-0MVFFJWPW007ZEPK** — installed/activated `.githooks/pre-push`
  (`core.hooksPath`), the gate this item hardens.
- **LP-0MVHSWUE80097KQJ** — earlier period where the gate did not run at all
  (`core.hooksPath` unset); explains some historic "no gate" observations.
- `docs/dev/git-hooks.md`, `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`,
  `skill/test_cache.py` (cache-key semantics), `tests/test_git_hooks.py`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (verified):** cache keys are path-independent (suite command +
  `HEAD` sha + dirty-content hash), so gating the same commit from another
  directory preserves cache reuse. Mitigation: assert this in the regression
  test.
- **Risk:** gating in a temporary detached worktree lacks untracked/ignored
  dependencies (`node_modules`, `.venv`, fixtures) → false red or wasted cold
  run. Mitigation: prefer gating in a checkout that already holds the commit
  (the worktree) or fail closed with an actionable message; never fail open.
- **Risk:** a stricter gate refuses legitimate pushes (e.g. operator pushes
  from a checkout that is intentionally behind). Mitigation: the refusal
  message must name the mismatch and the remedy; the test suite covers the
  happy path.
- **Risk:** touching the hook re-runs into the context-budget gate on the
  first `dev` push; keep hook text growth modest.
- **Risk (scope creep):** "gate every push at the pushed sha" invites a
  general gate rewrite. Extra opportunities (e.g. gating feature-branch
  pushes, redesigning `mirror_suite_cache`) are recorded as linked work items,
  not absorbed here.
- **Assumption:** the 2026-10-28 timing anomaly is *not* independently
  reproducible in a unit test; AC3's instrumentation is the intended way to
  make it diagnosable, and the gate-subject fix (AC1/AC2) removes the
  wrong-tree class regardless of that anomaly's cause.

---

# Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (OPEN QUESTION) — where should the fix land?** The item's ACs name
  `implement.py` changes, but `implement.py` is a SorraAgents framework file
  and this repo's worktrees cannot edit it.
  Options: **(a)** gate-side only — harden `.githooks/pre-push` in this repo so
  the gate refuses/gates the pushed commit (in-repo, testable here, also
  covers LP-0MVSJUM3O003C0H9); **(b)** pusher-side only — a SorraAgents (`SA-`)
  item changes `implement.py` to push from the worktree and surface hook
  stderr, and this `LP` item becomes a report/cross-reference; **(c)** both —
  gate-side hardening here plus a cross-linked `SA-` item for the pusher side.
  **Recommended:** (c) — each half lands in the repo that owns the file and
  gets its test where that repo's tests live.
  — Answer: *pending producer input.*
- **Q2 (OPEN QUESTION) — gate behaviour when the push cwd's `HEAD` is not the
  pushed commit.** Options: **(a)** gate the pushed commit transparently
  (e.g. temporary detached worktree at `local_sha`, or re-point the main
  checkout); **(b)** fail closed with an actionable message ("push from the
  worktree holding `<sha>`"); **(c)** gate transparently when possible, fail
  closed otherwise.
  **Recommended:** (c) — correct-by-default, and loud rather than silently
  wrong when the tree cannot be materialised.
  — Answer: *pending producer input.*
- **Q3 (resolved during intake, no producer input needed) — relationship to
  LP-0MVSJUM3O003C0H9.** Partial overlap only (different trigger: skipped
  fast-forward vs rebase-retry). This item is therefore scoped to the
  differences (retry path, gate evidence, retry-path regression test) and
  cross-linked; no duplicate item is created. Evidence: read both
  descriptions and the `implement.py` Step-5/Step-6/`_recover_non_fast_forward_push`
  code paths.
- **Q4 (resolved during intake) — is the cache key path-dependent?** No:
  `skill/test_cache.py::compute_git_state` hashes `HEAD` plus the *content* of
  dirty paths, and `cache_key` hashes the suite command + that state; the
  `--project-root` argument is not part of the key. Evidence: source read of
  `test_cache.py` (`compute_git_state`, `cache_key`) and
  `run_tests.py`/`audit_runner.py` cache-query call sites.

## Problem statement

The free-slot (direct-dispatch) admission guard in `proxy/proxy/provider.py` already records the governing decision reason verbatim for the deadline, deadline-relative safety-budget and flat cold-prefill-budget refusals (shipped with LP-0MVQ23API001UOET, commit `0466f5db`), but **no test pins that behaviour on the direct path**: the reason-contract tables drive only `eta_exceeds_budget_direct` through the free-slot route, so a regression could silently restore the 2026-10-25 retry-storm shape — a `Retry-After` advertised for a prompt that waiting cannot heal — whenever a local slot happens to be free.

## Users

- **Proxy operators / on-call engineers.** Story: *As an on-call engineer reading `local_admission_guard_direct_fallback` and a client `X-Local-Fallback-Reason`, I want the token to name the bound that actually refused local, so I can tell a temporal refusal (wait) from a permanent one (compact) without cross-referencing the guard's internal logic.*
- **Local-preferred clients (agents).** Story: *As an agent that is pinned local, I want a `prefill_budget_exceeded` refusal to say `retryable: false` and never hand me a `Retry-After`, so I compact my prompt instead of re-driving the same over-budget request in a retry loop.*
- **Proxy maintainers.** Story: *As a maintainer, I want both dispatch paths (queue and free-slot) covered by one table-driven contract, so adding a refusal reason cannot land with retry semantics on one path only.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Direct-path reason pass-through is table-driven and complete.** `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py` drives every admission-guard reason through the **free-slot** (direct) path end-to-end via `proxy_with_fallback` — `prefill_eta_exceeds_deadline`, `prefill_eta_exceeds_safety_budget`, `prefill_budget_exceeded`, and the ETA/budget case — asserting both `X-Local-Fallback-Reason` and body `reason` equal the governing decision reason, with `eta_exceeds_budget_direct` used only where the free-slot ETA/budget bound itself is the cause.
2. **A free-slot over-budget request refuses without a timer.** With a free local slot and a prompt above `local_cold_prefill_budget_tokens`, the end-to-end refusal through `proxy_with_fallback` carries `reason=prefill_budget_exceeded`, no `Retry-After` header, `retryable: false`, `suggested_action` naming compaction, and the token evidence (`new_tokens` / `budget_tokens`) on both headers and body.
3. **The governing reason reaches the recorded attempt and the dispatch log.** The `local_admission_reject` attempt diagnostics and the `local_admission_guard_direct_fallback ... reason=<token>` log line name the governing reason (not `eta_exceeds_budget_direct`) for the deadline, safety-budget and cold-budget refusals; the line still carries `free_slot=true`.
4. **Regression guard on the label.** A test fails if `eta_exceeds_budget_direct` is (re)emitted as the refusal reason for any non-ETA-budget decision reason, on either path.
5. **Docs verified/updated.** `proxy/docs/routing.md` (the "Local-only is enforced on every exit" exit table and the reason→retry-timing table) states that only the free-slot ETA/budget reason keeps the `eta_exceeds_budget_direct` token; any wording change lands with the code comments.
6. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes**, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries.
7. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Test-first, behaviour-preserving.** The mapping in `provider.py` (lines ~11938–11955) is believed correct; the deliverable is the pinning test set. If a test disproves the belief, fix the production code — do **not** weaken the test.
- **The client token vocabulary must not change for existing cases.** `eta_exceeds_budget_direct` stays the free-slot ETA/budget refusal token; it is pinned as a documented exit token by `proxy/tests/test_local_only_exit_docs.py` and the refusal-routing docs.
- **Do not disturb the too-large pin-decline contract** (LP-0MVSLZY470051ZB2 AC4): a pin-local client with a `prefill_budget_exceeded` / `context_too_large` verdict is promoted to the remote tiers rather than refused, so the free-slot over-budget *refusal* shape is observable on the exhaustion path (no fallback provider) — assert both shapes if both are reachable from the free-slot path.
- **No timing-contract changes.** `_refusal_retry_timing` / `NOT_TIME_RETRYABLE_REFUSAL_REASONS` (`provider.py` ~4498–4530) are the single source of retry semantics; assert through them, do not re-implement their arithmetic.
- No ad-hoc full-suite runs: use the test skill (`/skill:test`).

## Existing state

- `provider.py` free-slot guard branch (~11938–11955): `_direct_reason` is the decision reason verbatim when it starts with `prefill_eta_exceeds_deadline`, `prefill_eta_exceeds_safety_budget` or `prefill_budget_exceeded`, else the `eta_exceeds_budget_direct` dispatch label.
- `_prefill_admission_guard` (~7178–7291) applies the same rule to the single `local_admission_guard` log line via `log_label`.
- `_refusal_retry_timing` / `NOT_TIME_RETRYABLE_REFUSAL_REASONS` (~4498–4530) already give `prefill_budget_exceeded` and `context_too_large` no `Retry-After` and `retryable: false`; `_build_local_admission_reject_response` (~5673) and `_build_local_only_refusal_response` (~6670) both route through it.
- `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py` has the AC2/AC4 occupancy table (`_OCCUPANCY_REFUSAL_CASES`, ~1075–1150) and the cross-reason contract table (`_REFUSAL_CONTRACT_ROWS`, ~1450–1500) — but **only one direct-path row** (`eta_exceeds_budget_direct`); the `prefill_eta_exceeds_safety_budget` rows were routed through the queue path to reach the right reason.
- `proxy/tests/test_cold_prefill_budget.py` covers the free-slot guard one layer below routing (`test_direct_free_slot_guard_refuses_an_over_budget_request`, ~277) — a `_prefill_admission_guard` unit assertion, not the refusal contract.
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_eta_deadline.py` (~275–335) asserts the direct-path *log label* by re-deriving the label logic inline in the test (duplicated logic, no refusal-response assertion).
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` (~1248–1252, ~1337–1344) already documents the split ("the deadline/safety/budget reasons keep their own token").

## Desired change

Add free-slot rows to the reason-contract tables so each admission-guard reason is forced through the direct path, plus one end-to-end free-slot over-budget refusal test proving the no-timer/`retryable: false`/token-evidence contract; replace the inline label re-derivation in `test_prefill_eta_deadline.py` with a call through `_prefill_admission_guard` (or leave it and cover the gap in the contract table — implementer's call, documented in the commit).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — direct free-slot guard branch (`_direct_reason`, ~11938–11955) and `_prefill_admission_guard` `log_label` (~7262–7286); read-only unless a test disproves the mapping
- `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py` — occupancy case table (`_OCCUPANCY_REFUSAL_CASES`) and cross-reason contract table (`_REFUSAL_CONTRACT_ROWS`); add direct-path rows
- `proxy/tests/test_cold_prefill_budget.py` — free-slot over-budget end-to-end refusal contract
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_eta_deadline.py` — direct-path log-label tests (optionally de-duplicate against production logic)
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — exit table / retry-timing table wording

## Related work

- LP-0MVNTT4X8009IO2X — per-reason retry contract (parent of the 2026-10-25 retry-storm defect, AC1)
- LP-0MVQ23API001UOET — "Refactor: reason-aware timing decision for refusal paths": landed the `_direct_reason` pass-through in commit `0466f5db`
- LP-0MVQ23A6S007DVDM — "Test: AC2 — ETA/occupancy refusals return Retry-After + retry_at" (found this gap; had to route safety-budget cases through the queue path)
- LP-0MVSLZY470051ZB2 — too-large pin decline / promotion contract (AC4)
- LP-0MVIQ0F8T002FS42 — the original free-slot guard (`eta_exceeds_budget_direct` label)
- LP-0MVRMC275000R2W6 — `local_only_refused` logging of `_direct_reason`
- LP-0MVN4LBZ500281Z7 — flat cold-prefill budget (`prefill_budget_exceeded`)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (documented):** the production mapping in `provider.py` is already correct, so this item is a *test-pinning* task; if the first failing test disproves it, the fix lands here as well (still a bug item, no re-scope).
- **Assumption (documented):** `prefill_budget_exceeded` on the free-slot path reaches a *refusal* only on the exhaustion path (or via the refusal builders); for a pin-local client with a remote fallback the too-large verdict promotes instead. Tests must assert the shape that the free-slot route can actually produce.
- **Risk — test brittleness:** the occupancy table overrides are shared across rows; adding direct rows must not perturb the existing queue rows' expected `Retry-After` values.
- **Risk — duplicated label logic:** `test_prefill_eta_deadline.py` re-implements the guard's label rule in the test body, so a production regression can pass it. Prefer driving `_prefill_admission_guard` directly.
- **Risk — scope creep:** generalising the refusal tables or refactoring `_direct_reason` into a helper is tempting; record such opportunities as linked work items instead of widening this bug fix.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q: Is the code change still needed, or has the mapping already landed?**
  Answer (self-resolved, repo evidence): already landed. `git log -1 -S "prefill_eta_exceeds_safety_budget" -- proxy/proxy/provider.py` → `0466f5db` "LP-0MVQ23API001UOET: Implementation complete" (2026-10-28 11:07 UTC); the current branch (`dev`, `15aeabcc`) contains the `startswith(("prefill_eta_exceeds_deadline", "prefill_eta_exceeds_safety_budget", "prefill_budget_exceeded"))` branch at `provider.py:~11946`. Research: read the guard branch, `_prefill_admission_guard`'s `log_label` rule, `_refusal_retry_timing`, and both refusal builders; also confirmed `proxy/docs/routing.md` already documents the split. The item was therefore narrowed (partial duplicate of LP-0MVQ23API001UOET) to the still-missing **test coverage** — AC2/AC3 of the original brief.
- **Q: Which reasons must the direct path be tested with?**
  Answer (self-resolved, repo evidence): all four admission-guard reasons that the branch maps — `eta_exceeds_budget` (rendered as the `eta_exceeds_budget_direct` token), `prefill_eta_exceeds_deadline`, `prefill_eta_exceeds_safety_budget`, `prefill_budget_exceeded` — because `_REFUSAL_CONTRACT_ROWS` pins exactly that reason set. Source: `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py` (~1450–1580).
- **Q: Does the free-slot over-budget case need an end-to-end `proxy_with_fallback` test, given `test_cold_prefill_budget.py` already guards the decision?**
  Answer (self-resolved, repo evidence): yes — the existing test asserts only the `_prefill_admission_guard` return value, not the refusal contract (`Retry-After` absence, `retryable: false`, token evidence, `X-Local-Fallback-Reason`), which is what a client observes. Source: `test_cold_prefill_budget.py` ~277–296 vs. `_build_local_admission_reject_response` (~5673–5752).
## Related work (automated report)

- **LP-0MVNBJYE3003MF6J** – ETA-guard and prefill-deadline interaction review (blocked)
- **LP-0MVRCLPVI0057116** – Idle-admit eligibility must match prefill feasibility (measured 0/31 conversion) (open)
- **LP-0MVKUKEU80022C3U** – Deadline-aware local admission bound (completed)

## discovered-from:LP-0MVN44XB0009M33K

The **24 h AC4 verification** of resident-prefix admission
(`LP-0MVN44XB0009M33K`, window `2026-10-27T10:17:00Z → 2026-10-28T10:17:00Z`,
restart-free) could not attribute deadline cancellations because the residency
ladder logs every decision **unmeasured**: `analyze_proxy_usage.py` reports
`residency_decisions: 3607` with **measured ratio: 0 / no measurement: 3607**.
AC7 is explicit that "decisions logged but all unmeasured is a finding (ladder
not emitting), never a pass"; AC4 rule (a) (`reuse_ratio < 0.5`) is therefore
unevaluable for **all 99** window deadline events.

## Offending log extract (verbatim, window)

A resident (`session_slot`) admission that was *admitted*, yet carries
`n_past_actual=none` / `reuse_ratio=none`:

```
2026-10-27 11:02:06,334 - INFO - routing_resident_prefix provider=local model=Qwen3 decision=admit n_past_actual=none estimated_tokens=38222 reuse_ratio=none slot_owner_session=01a17d02-28a7-7023-88d6-065d86ede3d3 residency_source=session_slot min_ratio=0.50 tenants=none occupants=0 session=01a17d02-28a7-7023-88d6-065d86ede3d3
```

```
2026-10-27 11:05:44,948 - WARNING - prefill_deadline_exceeded session=01a17d02-28a7-7023-88d6-065d86ede3d3 deadline=120s → cancelling local dispatch and detouring to the next provider
2026-10-27 11:05:44,949 - ERROR - local_eviction_after_acceptance session=01a17d02-28a7-7023-88d6-065d86ede3d3 reason=prefill_deadline estimated_tokens=65881 new_tokens=17653 eta_prefill_s=93.0 elapsed_s=120.1 slot_id=unknown llama_task_id=unknown endpoint=http://localhost:8080
```

Value distribution over the window (all six overlapping log files):

| `reuse_ratio` / `n_past_actual` | count |
|---|---|
