## Goal (user story)

As an operator of the LLM proxy, I want the prefill-ETA admission guard to price local prefills at the rate they will actually achieve when the other slot is busy, so that admitted local dispatches convert to a first byte instead of burning the queue budget and falling back remote.

## Background / evidence (measured 2026-10-28, 23:30-00:38 + 00:00-00:38 windows)

- The local model served 15 of 1,883 streams; 1,152 routing skips and 487 admission-guard rejects occurred.
- The guard priced a 6,659-token prompt at `eta_prefill_s=13.9` (~479 t/s), yet the llama-server's own prompt-eval median is ~120 t/s (p25 85 / p75 202 / max 763, n=229 same day). Admission pricing runs 2-4x optimistic, at p95+ of the measured distribution.
- 2026-10-28 00:28:55: `decision=admit projected_wait_s=29.9 budget_s=60.0` with `busy_slots=1 in_flight_prefills=1 eta_occupancy_s=16.0`; queued the full 60 s, the gate never freed (occupant was a cold 65-89k-token audit prompt), then fell back remote — a guaranteed loss that admission was supposed to prevent. Retry was admitted again, dispatched after 13.4 s, and local immediately entered a ~480 s cooldown (dispatch failed).
- Root cause is not the gate serialisation structure (already priced as `eta * (busy_slots + 1)` plus a measured-occupant term): it is that (a) the rate calibration is unconditioned on co-residency — decode on the other slot halves prefill throughput (the single-prefill gate serialises prefills but not prefill+decode batching), and (b) the occupant-remaining term (`admitted_eta - elapsed`) inherits the optimistic rate and converges to ~0 for any occupant alive past its optimistic ETA, leaving the equally optimistic symmetric floor.

## Proposed fix

1. Maintain a separate rate distribution for contended prefills (observed while `busy_slots >= 1` / another slot generating) and price contended admissions against it; expose the chosen bucket on the decision log (e.g. `rate_bucket=contended`).
2. Rebase the occupant-remaining term on the occupant's remaining uncached new tokens priced at the contended rate, instead of `admitted_eta - elapsed`.
3. Pre/post measurement: log admission→first-byte conversion and abandoned-queue-wait share per new-token band to prove the fix.

## Scope guardrails

- Do NOT change `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` (60) or `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` (120) in this item; the ordering assertion 60 < 120 < 840 < 900 must stay intact.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: A contended decision (busy_slots >= 1) is priced with the contended rate bucket; unit test asserts the bucket and that `eta_occupancy` uses the occupant's remaining new tokens at that rate, never `admitted_eta - elapsed`.
- AC2: A simulated cold occupant with 60k remaining new tokens yields `eta_occupancy` >= contended-rate x remaining; the 6,659-token / 13.9 s case now projects >= median-rate prefill (>= 55 s at 120 t/s).
- AC3: Warm-prompt admissions are unaffected (cached_ratio path unchanged).
- AC4: Post-change, the share of queued local waits ending in `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue` drops below the 85% baseline measured 2026-10-19/20 over a 24 h window, with no new `local_eviction_after_acceptance` events.
- AC5: Full test suite green; existing prefill-ETA, deadline, occupancy and budget tests pass unchanged in intent.

## Related items

- LP-0MVKUKF65008D5UN Conservative prefill ETA for large prompts (percentile pricing >= 20k — the band floor this fix extends)
- LP-0MVICD2YW004DJPV Prefill-ETA admission guard ignores occupancy (symmetric floor origin)
- LP-0MVOFVCA2008DQVE Occupancy-aware deadline admission (measured-occupant term origin)
- LP-0MVKUKEU80022C3U Deadline-aware local admission bound (120 s deadline)
- LP-0MVGR2OXT0096OGK open: Measure whether lease_state/prefill_eta predict real local contention

## Plan (LP-0MVS8T6F4006DGG3, plan_complete 2026-10-28)

Decomposed into six deliverable children in **test-first dependency order**, plus
three `idea`-stage stubs created by the AC-coverage review (each restates one
parent AC; implement as part of the named child rather than separately — see
*Coverage stubs* below).

| # | Child | Type | Depends on | Covers |
|---|-------|------|-----------|--------|
| 1 | Pre-change admission-conversion baseline harness (LP-0MVS9Y7FG004QJ2S) | task | — | parent AC4 baseline (verification-first) |
| 2 | Contended prefill rate bucket (LP-0MVS9Y76R004B5M8) | feature | — | parent AC1 (bucket), AC2 (55 s case), AC3, AC5 |
| 3 | Occupant-remaining priced from new tokens at contended rate (LP-0MVS9YK9P006M1NQ) | feature | #2 | parent AC1 (`eta_occupancy`), AC2 (60k scenario), AC5 |
| 4 | Decision-log and usage-report surface for rate_bucket (LP-0MVS9YKHL007UBBZ) | feature | #1, #2, #3 | parent AC1 (log evidence), AC4 (observability) |
| 5 | Post-change 24h measurement window vs 85% baseline (LP-0MVS9Z0GY008LCJA) | task | #1, #2, #3, #4 | parent AC4 |
| 6 | Docs and rollback for contended pricing (LP-0MVS9Z034006MFZ6) | docs | #2, #3 | parent AC5 (documented rollback) |

Dependency graph: `1 → 4 → 5`, `2 → 3 → 4`, `2 → 6`, `3 → 6`, `1 → 5`, `2 → 5`, `3 → 5`.

### Vertical-slice phasing

Every child is a minimal end-to-end slice (production code + unit tests + log/report
surface + docs where the behaviour is operator-visible). There is no horizontal
"all the parsing first" phase: child 1 lands a complete, committable measurement
tool; child 2 lands a complete calibrated bucket incl. its decision-log field;
child 3 lands the occupant re-pricing incl. its tests; child 4 makes both visible
in the standard report; child 5 proves the outcome on live traffic.

Between phases: review the next child's description against what the previous
slice actually shipped, and update its description/ACs before starting it.

### Key implementation decisions (recorded for the implementer)

- **Co-residency evidence is OR'd, not inferred.** A sample is `contended` when
  the admission-time `busy_slots >= 1` snapshot on the dispatch record says so,
  **or** another session holds a live dispatch record for the same endpoint at
  first-byte time. Both signals are deterministic in tests; no heuristics, no
  wall-clock sampling.
- **Uncalibrated contended window falls back to the solitary window** and logs
  `rate_bucket=solitary_fallback`. Rationale: the guard's founding rule is
  "never reject on a guess"; a guessed contended slowdown multiplier would
  violate it. The log field makes the residual optimism visible instead.
- **Occupant rebase is token-based, not time-decayed**: `progress =
  min(1, elapsed / eta_prefill_s)`, `remaining_new = new_tokens * (1 - progress)`,
  `remaining_s = estimate(remaining_new, cached_ratio=0, contended=True)`.
  Records lacking `new_tokens`/`eta_prefill_s` contribute 0.0 (fail-open,
  byte-for-byte today's behaviour).
- **No new config knobs in this item**; the contended window reuses
  `local_admission_guard_min_samples`, and the documented rollback stays
  `local_admission_guard_policy: observe|off`.
- **Guardrails untouched**: `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` (60) and
  `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` (120); the `60 < 120 < 840 < 900` ordering
  assertion must keep passing.

### Coverage stubs (created by the AC-coverage review)

`LP-0MVSA3WOA002NAUH` (parent AC1), `LP-0MVSA3WWI00058T9` (parent AC3),
`LP-0MVSA3X5B008ZA88` (parent AC4) restate parent ACs whose wording differs from
the child ACs that cover them (coverage review matched them at 0.34/0.24/0.36).
They are **absorbed**: AC1 → children #2 and #3, AC3 → child #2 AC5, AC4 →
children #1 and #5. Do not implement them as separate work; close each as
absorbed when its covering child is complete.

### Effort and risk

Re-estimated after decomposition (supersedes the pre-plan `Extra Small` /
0.00 h placeholder estimate): **Medium effort, 21.6 h expected (range
20.0-42.0 h, 29.6 h recommended with overheads)**, risk **Medium (10/25)**,
confidence 85 %. The pre-plan estimate carried O=M=P=0.00 h (a degenerate
three-point input) and was not usable for scheduling.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Interview outcome: **no blocking questions** — the intake brief already specified
the goal, the three-part fix, the scope guardrails (60/120 unchanged) and five
testable ACs, and the six-child decomposition follows directly from them. Two
non-blocking questions are recorded for the operator; neither blocks
implementation.

- **OPEN QUESTION (directed to the operator, non-blocking) — AC4 is
  time-blocked.** Parent AC4 requires a 24 h *post-change* window. Decomposed as
  child #5 (LP-0MVS9Z0GY008LCJA), which can only run after the fix is deployed
  and a day of traffic has elapsed. Assumption recorded: parent AC4 is satisfied
  by child #5's committed measurement record, not by the implementation commits.
  Preferred option: **keep AC4 in this parent, gated by child #5**. Alternative:
  move AC4 wholesale into a follow-up measurement item and close the parent on
  AC1-AC3 + AC5. Source: this planning session; evidence: parent description,
  AC4 vs the `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue` baseline of 2026-10-19/20.
  Research: `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py` and
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/reporting.py` show no existing per-band
  conversion metric, hence child #1 lands the harness before any estimator change.
- **OPEN QUESTION (directed to the operator, non-blocking) — definition of
  "contended".** The plan defines a contended sample as *any* local prefill
  observed while another session holds a slot (prefill or decode), matching the
  measured mechanism (decode on the other slot halves prefill throughput).
  Preferred option: **co-residency (any other live slot holder)**, because the
  measured 2-4x gap is a batching effect, not a prefill-vs-prefill serialisation
  effect. Alternative: restrict the contended window to "another *prefill* is in
  flight". Source: this planning session; evidence: parent background —
  `local_max_concurrent_prefills: 1` serialises prefills, so prefill+prefill
  contention is already excluded by the gate, leaving prefill+decode as the
  observed contention. Research: `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`
  (`_get_live_prefill_in_flight_count`, `_live_prefill_remaining_seconds`) and
  `proxy/proxy/provider.py` (`_local_gate_occupancy`).

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-28 (plan session `herdr-1793200851-672483-3216`): six children created
  in test-first order with nine dependency edges; AC-coverage review ran
  (100 % covered, three idea-stage stubs created); effort/risk re-estimated to
  Medium/Medium (21.6 h expected); stage advanced to `plan_complete`, status
  `open`. Duplicate check: `wl search "contended"` — no completed or open item
  duplicating this scope (nearest: LP-0MVGR2OXT0096OGK, a measurement-only item
  on a different question).


## Delivery status (verified 2026-10-28 23:45 UTC)

All 13 attached children are terminal (`completed`/`in_review` or
`completed`/`done`), and their commits are ancestors of `origin/dev`
(`cc840d3d`, `91eab34d`, `9a866fc7`, `a843e62c`, `323fe680`, `bb4bcb3c`).

| AC | Verdict | Evidence |
|----|---------|----------|
| AC1 | met | Contended bucket in `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py` (`_contended_samples`, `rate_bucket`, `contended_samples`) priced via `estimate_prefill_seconds(..., contended=True)`; `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py:2129-2240` (`_live_prefill_remaining_seconds`) re-prices the occupant's remaining *uncached new tokens* at the contended rate — the `admitted_eta - elapsed` decay is gone. Pinned by `proxy/tests/test_prefill_eta_contended.py` and `proxy/tests/test_occupant_remaining_rebase.py`. |
| AC2 | met | `proxy/tests/test_occupant_remaining_rebase.py:121-161` (60k remaining new tokens ⇒ `occupancy >= 60_000 x contended_ms_per_token`) and `:165-181` (the 6,659-token case now asserts `projected_wait_s >= 55.0` and `eta_occupancy_s >= 55.0`, vs the measured 13.9 s). |
| AC3 | met | `proxy/tests/test_prefill_eta_contended.py:293-320` — `cached_ratio >= 0.9` keeps the pre-change solitary computation (contended selector suppressed on the warm path). |
| AC4 | **unmet — time-blocked** | Pre-change baseline committed (`docs/dev/prefill-admission-conversion.{md,json}`: 24 abandoned / 65 queued = 36.9 %). The post-change 24 h window needs the fix **deployed to the running proxy** (pid 3791954 started 2026-10-27 10:16 UTC, i.e. before the fix; harness output still shows `rate_buckets: {unknown: N}`, confirming the old code is serving) **plus** 24 h of post-deploy traffic. Tracked by `LP-0MVS9Z0GY008LCJA` (open, time-blocked; currently detached from this parent). |
| AC5 | met | `docs/dev/contended-prefill-pricing.md` (design + documented rollback via `local_admission_guard_policy: observe|off`); cached full suite green at HEAD: 6253 passed, 16 skipped, 11 xfailed. |

Guardrails untouched: `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` (60) and
`local_prefill_deadline_seconds` (120); no new config knobs.

### Release condition

This epic cannot reach `in_review` until AC4 is evidenced:

1. **Deployed — DONE 2026-10-29 00:10:18 UTC:** proxy restarted (pid
   1081749; `/health` healthy; llama + TTS up). Post-restart
   `local_admission_guard` decision lines carry `rate_bucket=` /

# Feature — Deterministic regression: in-request local re-dispatch after prefill-deadline cancellation

Child of LP-0MVPUBQLQ008GJOV. Extends the `proxy/tests/test_prefill_thrash_wedge.py`
injected-clock/stubbed-dispatcher harness so the 2026-10-26 10:41-10:47 incident
(a fresh dispatch lease acquired ~150 ms after `lease_released reason=prefill_deadline`,
gate held ~308 s, 3 `wedge_denials`) FAILS loudly on current code, and so the cause of
the un-engaged thrash gate is isolated before the fix child (C2) chooses its mechanism.
This is a test-first slice: no production code changes live here (test-only harness
extensions + a recorded cause determination).

## Target outcome

Deterministic, clock-injected reproduction of the post-deadline in-request local
re-dispatch and the un-engaged thrash gate; the harness pins WHICH gap the 2026-10-26
log exposure reflects (session-id arm/check-key mismatch vs a local dispatch path that
bypasses provider.py's local-branch gate) so the implementation child targets the real
mechanism.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1. A deterministic test (injected clock + stubbed local dispatcher mirroring
  `test_prefill_thrash_wedge.py`) asserts that a dispatch cancelled by
  `prefill_deadline_exceeded` is **not re-dispatched locally**: it simulates local
  dispatch → `prefill_deadline_exceeded` → `_release_prefill_deadline_dispatch` →
  same-session local re-dispatch attempt ~150 ms later, and asserts the re-dispatch does
  NOT acquire a fresh active lease (no `local_dispatch_denied` for other sessions from
  that record). Red on current code (pre-fix: fresh lease acquired post-release).
- AC2. The gate-engagement isolation test plants the thrash cooldown under the session
  id the refusing path actually resolves and asserts the local attempt is skipped
  (`routing_skip_local reason=prefill_thrash_cooldown`), covering the arm-key/check-key
  mismatch and the bypass-path hypotheses. It records which gap the incident exposed
  (comment on this item) for C2. Red on current code.
- AC3. The re-dispatch assertion also covers the marker: after the release,
  `local_prefill_in_flight` is cleared and `_extend_prefill_lease` cannot re-extend a
  stale in-flight marker (`lease_extended_during_prefill ... in_flight=True` must not
  appear for the cancelled dispatch).
- AC4. A ≤300 s hold-bound regression: a same-session re-acquisition (still permitted
  for legitimate long prefills) is bounded by the no-progress watchdog at ≤300 s
  simulated — fails if any hold chain exceeds 300 s (parent AC3).
- AC5. Full suite stays green with the new tests (deterministic injected clock; no real
  sleeps).
- AC6. A dispatch cancelled by `prefill_deadline_exceeded` is **not re-dispatched locally
  within the same request** (the detour goes to the next provider), **or** the
  re-dispatch is refused while the session's prefill-thrash cooldown is active — and the
  gate actually engages: the deterministic test (C1.AC1) fails on the pre-fix behaviour
  of a fresh lease acquired 150 ms after the release, satisfying parent
  LP-0MVPUBQLQ008GJOV AC1.
- AC7. Any hold that does remain is bounded by <=300 s (the epic's 5 min bound): a
  regression test asserts release within 300 s simulated (the no-progress watchdog must
  bound the record even when the session re-acquires), satisfying parent
  LP-0MVPUBQLQ008GJOV AC3 via C1.AC4.

## Constraints

- Mirror the existing harness determinism: injected monotonic clock, stub llama-server
  with stale `/slots` (`progress=None, alive=False`); no real sleeps.
- Do not weaken the no-progress watchdog (180 s) or the 10 s sweep cadence to make the
  bound pass.
- Test-only slice: no production behaviour change in this child.

## Risky assumptions

- The 2026-10-26 gap is a bypass path rather than an arm-key mismatch. Plan-log evidence
  (2026-10-28): the affected session's four post-deadline dispatches show NO
  `priority_routing`/`local_admission_guard`/`routing_check`/provider-cooldown logs
  before each `[local] POST`, while `local-qwen3 in cooldown` was globally active — i.e.
  requests reached `proxy_to_local` without the provider chain re-evaluating them; other
  sessions were consistently skipped. This favours a bypass path; the test must still
  decide formally.
- The harness can reproduce the ~150 ms post-release acquisition deterministically
  (clock injection covers it).

## Minimal implementation

1. Extend `proxy/tests/test_prefill_thrash_wedge.py` with a scenario: dispatch →
   deadline (injected clock) → `_release_prefill_deadline_dispatch` → immediate
   same-session re-dispatch attempt; assert lease table, denials, marker state.
2. Add the gate-engagement variant that re-dispatches through the observed bypass shape
   and asserts the skip engages; record the cause determination (comment) for C2.
3. Add the ≤300 s re-acquisition hold-bound test.
4. Run changed-scope tests via the test skill; full suite stays green.

## Key Files

- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_thrash_wedge.py`

# Feature — Enforce the post-deadline thrash gate at every local-dispatch entry; terminal in-request detour

Child of LP-0MVPUBQLQ008GJOV. Implementation slice: after the deterministic tests
(C1) pin the mechanism, make the cancelled session's claim on the local gate end with
the cancellation — the thrash-cooldown gate engages for EVERY local dispatch attempt
(including paths that bypass provider.py's chain gate), the same request does not
re-dispatch local after the deadline detour, and any remaining lease is bounded
≤300 s.

## Target outcome

A local dispatch cancelled by `prefill_deadline_exceeded` stops holding the local
dispatch gate: no in-request local re-dispatch acquiring a fresh lease ~150 ms after
the release; the per-session thrash cooldown demonstrably engages at every local
dispatch entry; `local_prefill_in_flight` never outlives the dispatch it marks; every
remaining hold is bounded ≤300 s (parent AC1-AC3).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1. Every path that can acquire a local dispatch lease consults the per-session
  thrash cooldown before acquisition — including direct local paths that bypass
  provider.py's chain gate (the shape C1's isolation test surfaced). A session whose
  cooldown is armed is refused (`routing_skip_local reason=prefill_thrash_cooldown`)
  with the chain falling to the next provider. C1's gate-engagement test goes green.
  Rollback knob `local_prefill_thrash_cooldown_seconds: 0` still disables the gate.
- AC2. The deadline detour is terminal for local within that request: a request-scoped
  marker set on `prefill_deadline_exceeded` prevents the same request from acquiring a
  fresh lease after release (the ~150 ms post-release fresh lease is impossible). C1's
  re-dispatch test goes green.
- AC3. After the cancellation the lease, `local_prefill_in_flight` marker are cleared
  BEFORE any retry, and the cancelled upstream prefill stream is closed (proven dead)
  so `_extend_prefill_lease` cannot re-extend from a stale marker (no
  `lease_extended_during_prefill ... in_flight=True` after release). C1's marker test
  goes green.
- AC4. Any remaining hold is bounded ≤300 s from its last progress for every
  acquisition path (deadline detour, same-session re-acquisition, active-expired
  sweep) without weakening the 180 s no-progress watchdog or the 10 s sweep cadence.
  C1's bound test goes green.
- AC5. Legitimate long prefills are unaffected: a live, progressing prefill keeps its
  lease (no-preemption same-session semantics preserved); first-byte latency stays
  inside `local_dispatch_max_prefill_seconds`; a successful local first byte clears
  the cooldown per the recovery-fraction rule (parent constraints).
- AC6. Changed-scope test gate passes and the full suite stays green with the fix.

## Constraints

- Do not weaken: the prefill deadline (120 s) detour-not-kill backstop, the
  no-progress watchdog (180 s), the 10 s sweep, the thrash cooldown (600 s / rollback
  knob 0), no-preemption same-session lease re-acquisition for genuine in-flight
  prefills.
- Scope: do NOT absorb lease-fairness renewal caps (LP-0MVOJ6KAW004EBV0) — record any
  overlap as related work, keep that item's scope there.
- Fix the mechanism C1 identifies (bypass and/or arm-key mismatch); a renewal cap alone
  is insufficient if the gate remains unengaged (parent AC1 mandates an engaged gate).

## Risky assumptions

- The incident re-dispatch is a same-request/retry client pattern (pi/opencode retries
  on 503); the request-scoped marker must not block unrelated concurrent requests from
  the same session (the session cooldown covers those).
- Closing the upstream prefill stream is sufficient to prevent stale-marker
  re-extension (verify with C1's marker test).

## Minimal implementation

1. Add a request-scoped post-deadline marker set in the `prefill_deadline_exceeded`
   path and checked at the lease-acquisition choke point; local is terminal for that
   request (chain falls to the next provider).
2. Consult the thrash cooldown at the single choke point every local dispatch passes
   (router.py `proxy_to_local` immediately before `_try_acquire_local_dispatch`) so
   direct bypass paths engage; keep the existing provider.py gate.
3. Harden the release path (deadline + measured-abort twins) so record + marker
   removal and upstream-stream close (bounded by `disconnect_cleanup_timeout`) complete
   before any retry can observe stale state.
4. Update code comments at the changed sites; keep the existing log vocabulary
   (`routing_skip_local`, `lease_released`, `prefill_thrash_cooldown_started`).

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/router.py` (`proxy_to_local`, `prefill_deadline_exceeded` block)
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` (`_try_acquire_local_dispatch`,
  `_release_prefill_deadline_dispatch`, `_release_unserved_dispatch`,
  `_prefill_thrash_cooldown_*`, `_extend_lease_during_prefill`)
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` (local branch + any direct dispatch paths C1 surfaces)
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_thrash_wedge.py` (harness extended by C1)
- Related: `proxy/proxy/ui.py` (`_dispatch_local_model_load` direct
  `srv.proxy_to_local`), per C1's cause comment

# Load-normalise the AC3 denial check in the idle-admit measurement

## Goal (user story)

As the operator, I want the AC3 `local_dispatch_denied` check normalised to
window load (per bypass/fallback event), so the measured `+9.3 %` per-hour
denial "increase" (window 2026-10-22 21:48 → 2026-10-23 21:48, ~2× busier than
the before window) is judged on a load-independent signal instead of a
confounded raw rate.

## Measured evidence (artifact `docs/dev/idle-window-measurement-2026-10-22-to-2026-10-23.json`)

| Metric | Before | After | Δ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `local_dispatch_denied` raw | 66.0 /h | 72.1 /h | **+9.3 %** (> 5 % band → fail) |
| `large_context_bypass` events | 1,790 | 3,702 | +107 % |
| Remote fallback events | 6,953 | 12,888 | +85 % |
| Denials per bypass+fallback event | 1,584/8,743 = 0.181 | 1,731/16,590 = 0.104 | −42 % |

The raw rate cannot distinguish "the override causes more denials" from "a 2×
heavier window produces proportionally more denials". The tool currently
implements only the raw per-hour rate (`scripts/idle_admit_impact.py`:
`denied_before_rate`/`denied_after_rate`, `_DENIED_TOLERANCE_PCT = 5.0`).

## Acceptance criteria

- `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py` reports a load-normalised denial rate — denials per bypass+fallback event — alongside the existing per-hour rate, in both the AC3 check and the JSON/markdown output.
- The AC3 verdict uses the normalised rate for pass/fail (the raw per-hour rate remains reported), so a raw increase caused purely by higher load no longer fails the check; a genuine per-event increase still fails.
- Tests cover: the normalised-rate arithmetic against the exact window numbers above (fail → pass), a synthetic per-event denial increase that still fails the check, and backward compatibility of all existing JSON keys and exit codes.
- Re-running the tool `--window-closed` on the closed window records the AC3 verdict on LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD next to the baselines table, with the normalised numbers and sample counts.
- `docs/dev/idle-window-measurements.md` documents the normalised metric definition and why the raw per-hour rate is load-confounded.

## Key Files

- `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py`
- `tests/test_idle_admit_impact.py`
- `docs/dev/idle-window-measurements.md`

# tree_coverage AC extraction truncates hard-wrapped bullets (false coverage "stop")

Discovered from: LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD — while planning that item, the shared
AC-coverage review reported every parent AC as uncovered with `recommendation:
"stop"`, even though the children (LP-0MVJXGSEG0045IAF, LP-0MVRCLPVI0057116)
clearly cover the scope.

## Root cause

`extract_acceptance_criteria()` in `skills/shared/tree_coverage.py` treats each
physical line as one AC. The project's descriptions hard-wrap AC bullets at
~80 columns, so a single bullet like "A ≥24 h post-deploy window is analysed
with `proxy-usage-analysis` and reports, next to the baselines above: ..." is
cut to its first fragment ("...and reports,"). Similarity matching against
child ACs (also wrapped) then scores 0.05–0.18, below the 0.2 auto-close
floor, and every AC is reported uncovered (coverage 0 %, recommendation
"stop"). Re-flowing the AC text into single lines restores full sentences but
the matcher still cannot see the mapping because both sides are truncated.

## Impact

- False `stop` results block stage advancement on wrapped items (LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD
  sat `intake_complete` while its measurement work was already recorded).
- Coverage % is meaningless (0 %) for well-maintained wrapped descriptions.
- Auditors/planners must manually re-verify coverage on every wrapped item.

## Acceptance criteria

- `extract_acceptance_criteria()` joins wrapped continuation lines of a bullet
  into a single AC entry instead of truncating at the first line (indented
  sub-list markers still excluded as before).
- A regression test covers a hard-wrapped multi-line AC bullet and asserts one
  complete AC is returned.
- Re-running coverage review on LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD after the fix no longer
  reports all 5 parent ACs as uncovered (score movement is what matters, not
  a specific threshold).

## Key Files

- `skills/shared/tree_coverage.py` (agent infrastructure — do not edit without
  operator approval; the fix itself is a separate authorised change)
- `skills/plan/tests/`

Measured 2026-10-27 16:16 → 2026-10-28 15:55 (24h post-payload window) by the deterministic analysis CLI: the published prefill_eta_seconds does **not** predict real prefill duration for dispatches that ran.

Evidence: /home/rgardler/proxy-usage-reports/report.md — 'Local contention prediction vs reality' M3 table.
- Predicted (status_request polls): p50 = 91.6 s (n=10,618), p90 = 124.2 s
- Observed (llama-server prompt eval time): p50 = 2.4 s (n=901), p90 = 27.7 s
- Signed error (pred − obs): p50 +89.3 s (relative +3865%), p90 +96.5 s (relative +348%)
- Verdict: over_predicts (tolerance 25%)

Why it matters: the ETA is the cache-cold reference-prompt cost used by admissions and published to dispatchers (status_estimate, proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py). A dispatcher pacing on the published ETA will refuse work that would actually be served quickly — i.e. the signal over-refuses servable local work. The reference prompt appears systematically far larger than the median served prompt.

Open question for calibration: should the ETA be calibrated to the observed distribution (e.g. prompt-size-banded calibration), or relabelled as a worst-case bound, or budgeted per-request? See LP-0MVGDUV5E005UWBQ / LP-0MVODJ3P6000AIUM for the calibration lineage.

Known limitation: llama-server eval lines carry no per-line timestamp, so the comparison is quantile-matched (p50/p90 of each distribution), not per-dispatch pairing (documented in REFERENCE.md Limitations).

# Test: local-preferred behaviour matrix

Parent: LP-0MVSHWL47000EVJY.

## Goal

Pin the whole contract in one table-driven regression suite so future routing work cannot silently revert to "hard 429" or "silent remote".

## Matrix

| Preference | Slot | Verdict | Expected |
|---|---|---|---|
| absent / `prefer-local` | free | — | local (unchanged) |
| absent / `prefer-local` | busy | deferrable | remote fallback (unchanged) |
| `remote-ok` | — | — | local removed from chain, remote serves (unchanged) |
| `local-preferred` | free | — | local |
| `local-preferred` | busy | deferrable | queue → retryable 429, **no** remote dispatch |
| `local-preferred` | busy | too_large | remote serves, **no** local-capacity 429 |
| `local-only` (legacy) | busy | deferrable | identical to `local-preferred` |
| any | — | remote-less chain (`private` model) | unchanged |

## Deliverables

- Extend `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py`, `proxy/tests/test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` (rename semantics or add a sibling file) and `proxy/tests/test_admission_reserve.py` with the matrix above.
- Each row asserts: HTTP status, `X-Local-Route`, `X-Provider` / served entry, the presence or absence of remote dispatch (spy on `proxy_to_remote`), and for deferrals the retry fields.
- A named regression reproducing the 2026-10-28 incident numbers (`eta_prefill_s=31.7`, `projected_wait_s=63.4`, `budget_s=60.0`, `new_tokens=6627`, `budget_tokens=25000`) asserting `deferrable` + retryable 429 + zero remote calls.

### Per-row assertion detail (makes AC1/AC4 decidable)

| Matrix row | Home | Additional assertions |
|---|---|---|
| absent / `prefer-local`, free | `test_admission_reserve.py` (vocabulary rows) + `test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` (existing exit rows) | `X-Local-Route: local`, local provider name in `X-Provider`, zero remote calls; response shape byte-identical to today (no `retryable`, no `verdict` field) |
| absent / `prefer-local`, busy, deferrable | `test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` (existing exit rows) | remote provider serves, `X-Local-Route: remote`, local neither dispatched nor refused |
| `remote-ok`, any | `test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` (`test_remote_ok_still_strips_local_entries`) | local entry absent from the resolved chain (`apply_local_preference` output), remote serves |
| `local-preferred`, free | `test_local_admission_guard.py` (`_free_slot_cfg`) | served locally, `X-Local-Route: local`, no queue entry, no 429 |
| `local-preferred`, busy, deferrable | `test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` (preference axis on every exit row) + `test_local_admission_guard.py` | 429, `X-Local-Route: refused`, `X-Local-Fallback-Reason` set, `retryable: true`, `Retry-After`/`retry_at` pair, body verdict `deferrable`, **zero** `proxy_to_remote` calls |
| `local-preferred`, busy, too_large | `test_local_admission_guard.py` (`_cold_budget_cfg` + over-budget prompt) | remote serves, **no** 429, no `X-Local-Route: refused`, local removed from chain |
| `local-only` (legacy), busy, deferrable | `test_admission_reserve.py` (`parse_preference` row) + matrix rows above re-run under the alias | normalises to `local-preferred`; identical status/headers/retry fields to the `local-preferred` row, one deprecation log line per request |
| any, remote-less chain (`private`) | `test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` (`no_local_route` row family) | deferral unchanged (retryable 429 per A5), never promoted, no remote entry to dispatch to |

## Dependency & sequencing

- Depends on LP-0MVSHWYVE005MS16 (vocabulary), LP-0MVSHX47F003XEIZ (verdict) and LP-0MVSHXTLS000VMLE (chain/deferral). All three are still `open`/`blocked` as of the 2026-10-28 planning run, so this item stays `blocked` and is implemented **last** in the epic.
- Row expectations are *owned* by those three items: the verdict vocabulary (`deferrable` / `too_large`), the retryable-429 field names and headers, and the per-exit-path list all come from them. Re-read their descriptions and the landed code before writing assertions; do not re-derive the vocabulary here — import the production constants/helper so a rename in the owning item fails loudly in one place instead of drifting.
- Test-first ordering is satisfied at epic level: each prerequisite child lands its own tests with its slice (decision 2 in LP-0MVSHWL47000EVJY). This item is the cross-cutting matrix that asserts *already-implemented* behaviour; writing it first would deadlock the dependency graph.

## Existing state (reuse, do not duplicate)

- `proxy/tests/test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` — `_ExitRow` table, one row per exit from the local route (`thrash_cooldown`, `router_skip_physical_cap`, `router_skip_economic`, `router_skip_residency`, `router_skip_tenancy`, `queue_depth_cap`, `queue_wait_expiry`, `admission_guard_free_slot`, `entry_context_cap`, `quota_hard_stop`, `chain_cooldown`, `no_local_route`), each a `pytest.param` asserting 429 + `X-Local-Route: refused` + `X-Local-Fallback-Reason` + no upstream call. Its module docstring already explains the matrix design and records that the `xfail(strict=True)` machinery was retired when the choke point landed.
- `proxy/tests/test_admission_reserve.py` — reserve/verdict unit rows plus the existing remote spy `patch("proxy.server.proxy_to_remote", _remote)` (≈ lines 443, 489, 530, 604, 642); `test_unknown_preference_value_falls_back_to_prefer_local` is the vocabulary row to extend.
- `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py` — guard suite with `_guard_patches()`, `_free_slot_cfg()`, `_cold_budget_cfg()`, `_OccupancyRefusalCase`, `_RefusalContractRow` and `test_refusal_contract_table_has_exactly_one_row_per_reason`; the incident regression belongs beside these.
- `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_retry_docs.py` — parses the documented retry contract (`_contract_rows()`, `_documented_timing()`) and already asserts `test_local_only_is_documented_as_refusal_not_remote_fallthrough`; new doc/contract assertions follow this shape.
- Spy hooks for "no remote dispatch": `patch("proxy.server.proxy_to_remote", ...)` at reserve level and `patch("proxy.provider._get_proxy_to_remote", ...)` at dispatch-loop level (pattern in `proxy/tests/test_chain_hold.py`).

## Reuse and implementation notes

- Reuse the exit-path table: add a **preference axis** (legacy `local-only` alias and `local-preferred`) to `_EXIT_ROWS` instead of restating the exits in a second table — a duplicated exit description is exactly the drift this matrix exists to catch.
- No rename of `test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py`: renaming breaks citations in `proxy/docs/routing.md`, sibling work items and the retry-docs assertions for no behavioural gain. Retitle its module docstring to "local-pinned refusal matrix (`local-preferred`, legacy `local-only` alias)".
- Tests must not re-implement the verdict or the ETA: call the production helper (`local_capacity_verdict(...)`, `evaluate_admission(...)`) and the production retry-timing helper and assert on their outputs. Only the incident regression pins literal numbers (taken from the 2026-10-28 log lines); every other row derives from config plus the calibrated seed.
- Every row is its own `pytest.param(..., id=...)` with row-specific expectation fields, so a red row names the behaviour that broke (AC1). Parametrised ids compose the preference with the exit or verdict (e.g. `local-preferred-busy-deferrable`, `local-only-legacy-busy-deferrable`) so a red parameter reads as behaviour, not implementation (AC4); the existing per-exit ids stay unchanged to avoid churn in the 12 landed rows.
- Keep the existing convention of each touched file: table + one structural counter-case, module docstring naming the owning work item.
- Changed-scope selection: `run_tests.py`'s `map_changed_to_tests()` selects a changed test file directly, so `/skill:test --scope changed` picks these three files up with no extra registration (AC3).

## Open question (advisory, non-blocking)

- The 429 body key carrying the verdict (`verdict` vs `local_capacity_verdict`) is owned by LP-0MVSHX47F003XEIZ, which has not landed. Resolution for this item: assert through the production payload builder / its exported constant rather than a literal string, so whichever name that child ships is pinned without introducing a second source of truth. Revisit only if that child's field name turns out not to be importable.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1 Every matrix row is a test with its own assertions (no shared assertion that hides which row regressed).
- AC2 The incident regression asserts zero remote dispatch.
- AC3 The suite runs in the changed-scope gate and the full suite stays green.
- AC4 Test names state the behaviour (not the implementation detail) so the matrix is readable without reading code.
- AC5 All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments and docstrings; operator-facing docs (`docs/`, `proxy/config.yaml` commentary) are tracked in LP-0MVSHXU8E004BL57.
- AC6 Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/tests/test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` — per-exit-path rows: no remote dispatch, retryable-429 fields, `X-Local-Route`.
- `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py` — admission-guard rows (free slot, deferrable busy, too-large promotion) plus the 2026-10-28 incident regression.
- `proxy/tests/test_admission_reserve.py` — vocabulary/verdict rows (`local-preferred`, legacy alias, unknown/absent fallback).
- `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_retry_docs.py` — doc/contract assertions that keep the documented retry fields in step with the tests.

# Docs: local-preferred semantics, wire compatibility and client migration

Parent: LP-0MVSHWL47000EVJY. Depends-on: LP-0MVSHXTLS000VMLE (chain/deferral — the documented behaviour must be the shipped behaviour).

## Goal

Document the replacement of `local-only` by `local-preferred` everywhere an operator or client author looks, so an operator reading `proxy/docs/routing.md` or `proxy/config.yaml`, and a client author reading the retry contract, sees `local-preferred` as the canonical pin-local value and knows exactly what a retryable 429 asks of them.

## Deliverables

- `proxy/config.yaml` commentary for `X-Local-Preference` (the guard/reservation/preference block around `:1925`): describe the three effective behaviours (`prefer-local` default, `local-preferred` pin-with-deferral, `remote-ok` strip), the too-large promotion rule, and the counted-but-deprecated `local-only` alias.
- `proxy/config.yaml` `private` model comment (`:402-403`): state that a remote-less chain still defers (unchanged) and that `local-preferred` needs remote tiers to promote.
- The routing doc (`proxy/docs/routing.md` — the operator-facing routing document; root `README.md:267` points there and no separate `docs/local-admission*` file exists): add a short "local-preferred" section, the deferral/retry contract (retryable 429 with `Retry-After`/`retry_at`), the too-large promotion rule with its thresholds, and the 2026-10-28 incident shape as a worked example.
- Migration note: clients may keep sending `local-only`; the herdr/pi-extension rename is tracked in the ContextHub store; end-to-end deferral also needs the client to honour the retryable 429 (WL-0MVSBF5XZ001H7V7).
- Update stale documentation comments that describe `local-only` as the only local-pinning value (`admission_reserve.py`, `priority.py`, `provider.py` docstrings/comments).
- Move the prose assertion in `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_retry_docs.py` with the prose it pins (see AC6).

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1 No operator-facing doc or `config.yaml` comment still presents `local-only` as the primary/supported value without naming `local-preferred` as canonical. Verified by `grep -n "local-only" proxy/docs/routing.md proxy/config.yaml`: every remaining occurrence is in deprecated-alias context (states the alias is accepted and normalised).

## Problem statement

When `implement.py finish` cannot fast-forward the main checkout to the commit it is
about to push (main checkout dirty from concurrent work), it logs a warning and pushes
anyway from that stale checkout. The `dev`/`main` push then runs `.githooks/pre-push`
with `--project-root <main checkout>` — so the full suite is measured against the *old*
working tree, and the result is cached under the *old* git-state fingerprint
(`HEAD` + dirty content). The push returns green in seconds without the pushed commit
ever being verified: a silent fail-open in the only full-suite enforcement point for
`dev`.

## Users

- **Agent implementers** running `implement.py finish` in a repo with a busy main
  checkout: they need a push that is either genuinely verified or loudly refused, never
  a green gate that proves nothing.
- **Producers / release reviewers** relying on `run_tests.py --summary` as the
  "the pushed commit was full-suite green" evidence trail.
- Example story: *As a producer reviewing a `dev` push, I want a green gate to mean the
  pushed commit's tree passed the full suite, so that I can trust `dev` without
  re-running the suite manually.*

## Acceptance criteria

- A `dev`/`main` push issued while the checked-out tree is **not** the pushed commit
  (dirty main checkout ⇒ skipped Step-5 fast-forward) either verifies the pushed commit
  itself or **fails closed**; it never reports green using evidence from a different
  tree.
- The gate's diagnostic (refusal message and/or finish output) names **both** the pushed
  commit (`local_sha`) and the tree/SHA actually under test, so the next operator knows
  which tree was verified.
- On the gated path, the suite run is keyed to the pushed commit (`run_tests.py
  --summary` reports a cached green entry at that commit), not to the stale checkout.
- A regression test reproduces "dirty main checkout + skipped fast-forward" in the
  existing hermetic hook sandbox and asserts the pushed commit is the tree under test
  (or that the push is refused), while the existing green `dev`-push test still passes.
- At least one test/validation criterion is covered by the repo suite; all related
  documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and
  any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Repository boundary (open — see Q1).** The observable defect spans two owners:
  the repo-local hook + its tests (this repo, `projects/llm`) and the framework
  (`~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/implement.py` Step 5/6, canonical hook copies
  in `projects/SorraAgents`). Framework/agent-infrastructure files may not be edited
  without explicit authorisation; the default scope here is the repo-local hook and its
  regression test, with the framework change recorded as a linked follow-up.
- `.githooks/pre-push` must stay POSIX `sh` with no new runtime dependencies (it runs
  inside `git push` for every consumer of this repo).
- Feature-branch pushes must keep skipping the suite (fast loop unchanged) — the guard
  applies only to `refs/heads/dev` and `refs/heads/main` targets.
- The existing escape hatches (`TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1`, `--no-verify`) keep working.
- Cache plumbing stays fail-soft: mirroring must never decide a push's outcome.

## Existing state

- `.githooks/pre-push` already reads all four stdin fields per pushed ref
  (`local_ref local_sha remote_ref remote_sha`) but uses only `remote_ref`; `local_sha`
  is discarded, so the gate cannot tell which commit it is supposed to verify.
- The gate runs `run_tests.py --scope full --strict-git-env --project-root "$repo_root"`
  with `repo_root="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"` — i.e. the checkout `git push`
  runs in, which `implement.py finish` makes the **main checkout**.
- `test_cache.compute_git_state()` fingerprints `HEAD` + the content of every dirty path,
  so a stale-but-dirty main checkout produces a *valid, different* fingerprint; a
  previous green run for that same stale+dirty state is a legitimate cache hit → the gate
  returns green in seconds.
- `implement.py` Step 5 fast-forwards the main checkout's `dev` to the new commit
  precisely so the hook sees the new files; on failure it only logs
  `"Fast-forward dev failed (%s); push will proceed from the stale checkout — the
  context-budget gate may reject the push."` and continues to Step 6
  (`git_push_to_dev(repo_root, …)`).
- Observed 2026-10-28 (LP-0MVRMC1AD0013HND): main checkout dirty (8 unrelated paths),
  fast-forward skipped, main `dev` stayed at `7393ef14`, push landed `11870e99`; gate
  green in seconds; `run_tests.py --summary` reported `missing` for the pushed commit;
  a throwaway worktree at the pushed commit gave 6136 passed / 0 failed.
- Existing coverage: `tests/test_git_hooks.py` (13 hermetic sandbox tests, fake runner,
  behavioural assertions) — its `_hook()` helper always sends `HEAD` as `local_sha`, so
  no test can express "pushed commit ≠ checked-out tree".

## Desired change

Gate the pushed commit, not "whatever is checked out". Two acceptable shapes (the
author's acceptance criteria allow either; see Q2 for the recommendation):

1. **Fail closed (preferred default).** In the `dev`/`main` gate block, compare
   `git rev-parse HEAD` in the gate's project root with the gated `local_sha`. On
   mismatch, refuse the push with an actionable message naming the pushed commit, the
   checked-out SHA, the tree path, and the recovery instructions (re-run
   `implement.py finish` once the main checkout is clean, or verify the commit in a
   worktree and re-push). Never execute the suite for the wrong tree.
2. **Gate the pushed commit itself.** Check out `local_sha` into a throwaway detached
   worktree and run the suite with `--project-root <worktree>`, mirroring the cache entry
   back (the hook already has `mirror_suite_cache`). Unblocks concurrent work at the cost
   of worktree lifecycle inside a hook.

Either way, the diagnostic must name the tree measured, and `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` must
describe the behaviour with a copy-pasteable reproduction.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.githooks/pre-push` — capture the gated `local_sha` per `refs/heads/dev|main` ref in
  the stdin loop (currently discarded), then guard/redirect the gate; extend the
  refusal message; reuse `mirror_suite_cache` if option 2 is chosen.
- `tests/test_git_hooks.py` — add a `local_sha` override to `_hook()` (reuse `_sandbox`,
  `_install_runner`, `_marker`); new regression test "stale checkout ≠ pushed commit is
  refused / gated against the pushed commit"; assert the fake runner is not invoked for
  the stale tree.
- `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` — document pushed-commit verification, the refusal, the
  `run_tests.py --summary` verification step, and the dirty-main-checkout reproduction.
- `scripts/install_git_hooks.sh` — no change expected (it only sets `core.hooksPath` and
  fixes the exec bit); confirm it stays a no-op for the new logic.
- Framework follow-up (only if Q1 authorises it — outside this repo):
  `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/implement.py` (Step 5 fast-forward ~5141–5216,
  Step 6 push ~5235, finish report), `~/.pi/agent/skills/test_cache.py::compute_git_state`,
  and the canonical hook copies in `~/projects/SorraAgents/.githooks/pre-push`.

## Related work

- **LP-0MVRNFW0B00382D3 — "Investigate: dev-push full-suite gate can validate the wrong
  tree on the non-fast-forward retry path" (open, bug).** *Partial overlap — duplicate
  check performed.* Its AC1 already states the general invariant ("a mismatch between
  the push cwd's `HEAD` and the pushed `local_sha` must never silently verify the wrong
  tree: gate it correctly or refuse with an actionable message") and AC3/AC4 require
  observable gate evidence plus a `HEAD` ≠ pushed-sha regression test. This item owns the
  **skipped-fast-forward / dirty-main-checkout** trigger and its concrete reproduction;
  the two triggers want the *same* hook guard, so implementing both separately would
  duplicate the fix (see Q2).
- LP-0MVSJUM3O003C0H9's discovering item: LP-0MVRMC1AD0013HND (post-push verification
  surfaced the gap).
- LP-0MVHSWUE80097KQJ — "Pre-push full-suite gate not wired in this checkout
  (`core.hooksPath` unset)" — the gate's activation history and the same
  `run_tests.py --summary` = `missing` signal.
- LP-0MVFFJWPW007ZEPK — activated `core.hooksPath` and pinned the context-budget
  thresholds (the gate family this item hardens).
- `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` — the gate's contract, escape hatches and the
  "simulate a `dev` push" recipe.
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` (framework) — `implement.py finish` pushes from the
  main checkout by design; the reason a worktree-push alternative needs authorisation.

## Risks & assumptions

- *Risk: fail-closed blocks routine finishes* on hosts where the main checkout is
  routinely dirty (this host, 2026-10-28). Mitigation: the refusal message names the
  one-step recovery, and option 2 (gate in a worktree) is available. Assumption: a
  fail-closed push is acceptable engineering behaviour for a release gate.
- *Risk: HEAD equality alone is not enough* — a clean-HEAD but dirty tree still measures
  a tree that differs from the pushed commit (an uncommitted edit can mask a red
  commit). Open question Q3.
- *Risk (option 2): worktree creation inside a pre-push hook* can deadlock with
  `implement.py`'s own worktree lifecycle and doubles checkout/dependency handling.
- *Risk: scope creep into the framework.* Extra opportunities (finish-report wording,
  pushing from the worktree, propagating the guard to every consumer repo's hook copy)
  are recorded as linked follow-up items, not folded into this item.
- *Assumption: the cache fingerprint semantics stay as-is* (HEAD + dirty content);
  the gate must work with them rather than redefining the cache key.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Evidence gathered before asking (so the questions are not repo-search answerable):
`.githooks/pre-push` discards `local_sha`; `test_cache.compute_git_state()` keys on
`HEAD` + dirty content; `implement.py` Step 5 only *warns* when the fast-forward is
skipped and still pushes from `repo_root`; `tests/test_git_hooks.py::_hook()` always
sends `HEAD` as `local_sha`; the main checkout of this repo is currently clean.

- **Q1 (shape + scope).** Which fix shape, in which repository?
  - A: repo-local fail-closed guard in `.githooks/pre-push` — refuse a `dev`/`main` push
    when the checkout's `HEAD` ≠ the gated `local_sha`, naming both SHAs, the tree path
    and the recovery step; regression test in `tests/test_git_hooks.py`; framework
    improvement filed as a linked follow-up.
  - B: repo-local "gate the pushed commit" — check out `local_sha` in a throwaway
    detached worktree inside the hook, run the suite with `--project-root <worktree>`,
    mirror the cache entry (`mirror_suite_cache`) so the entry lands at the pushed
    commit.
  - C: framework change only (`implement.py`: push from the worktree / verify the pushed
    commit / name the verified tree in the finish report) — requires explicit
    authorisation to edit agent-infrastructure files, tracked under a SorraAgents item.
  - **Recommended:** A — smallest deterministic change, testable in the existing hermetic
    sandbox, no worktree lifecycle inside a git hook, and it composes with B or C later
    (the guard is the invariant; B/C are the unblocking refinements).
  - Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** (producer).
- **Q2 (overlap with LP-0MVRNFW0B00382D3).** That open item already requires "`HEAD` ≠
  pushed `local_sha` must never silently verify the wrong tree" for the non-fast-forward
  retry path; this item's guard would satisfy both. Consolidate, or keep two items?
  - A: transfer this item's distinct ACs (dirty-main-checkout reproduction test;
    cache entry keyed to the pushed commit) onto LP-0MVRNFW0B00382D3 and close this item
    as a duplicate.
  - B: keep both, implement the shared guard once under whichever is scheduled first, and
    record a `Blocks`/related link so the second becomes verification only.
  - **Recommended:** B — the triggers are distinct regression scenarios (retry path vs
    dirty checkout) worth naming in tests, but only one implementation should exist.
  - Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** (producer).
- **Q3 (strictness).** When `HEAD` *does* equal the pushed `local_sha` but the tree is
  dirty (foreign edits, untracked files), should the gate still run?
  - A: yes — run it, but warn loudly that the tree is not the pushed commit.
  - B: refuse — a dirty tree's fingerprint can never match the pushed commit's clean
    fingerprint, so `run_tests.py --summary` at the pushed commit stays `missing` and the
    evidence trail (AC3) is unmet.
  - **Recommended:** B, excluding any project-declared expected-dirty paths (none are
    declared for this repo); the main checkout is clean at intake time, so a clean-tree
    precondition is not a routine blocker here.
  - Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** (producer).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MVRNFW0B00382D3** – Investigate: dev-push full-suite gate can validate the wrong tree on the non-fast-forward retry path (open)
- **LP-0MVHSWUE80097KQJ** – Pre-push full-suite gate not wired in this checkout (core.hooksPath unset) (completed)
- **LP-0MVFFJWPW007ZEPK** – Install the .githooks/pre-push gate (core.hooksPath) so the dev-push full-suite gate actually runs (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: ac1, ac3, ac4, acceptance, acs (+358 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_nothink.txt` — matched: ac1, ac3, ac4, acceptance, acs (+358 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_think.txt` — matched: ac1, ac3, ac4, acceptance, acs (+358 more)

# Feature: `local-preferred` pin across every local-route exit

Parent: LP-0MVSHXTLS000VMLE. Depends on: LP-0MVSHWYVE005MS16 (preference vocabulary — canonical `PREF_LOCAL_PREFERRED`, alias normalisation) and LP-0MVSHX47F003XEIZ (capacity verdict feature, incl. its children LP-0MVSL7QJW006OYPB `local_capacity_verdict()` and LP-0MVSL7SDV007XVG6 wiring).

## Goal

A `local-preferred` request whose capacity verdict is `deferrable` is never handed to a non-local provider, whichever way the local route exits — admission refusal, lease denial, slot exhaustion, context/`resident_prefix` skip, stall, empty response or sibling-failure — on **both** dispatch cycles. This is today's `local-only` guarantee, expressed on the new canonical value and gated by the verdict instead of by the raw header value.

This slice is the *pin* half of the parent feature: it decides **whether** a non-local dispatch may happen. Deferral (queue-budget expiry → retryable 429) is LP child "deferral"; chain-level stripping of local on `too_large` and the promoted log line are LP child "too-large promotion"; the single per-request outcome line is LP child "routing-outcome line".

## Deliverables

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`:
  - One request-scoped pin predicate (e.g. `_local_preference_pins_local(request, preference) -> bool`) returning `True` only when the resolved preference is the canonical pin-local constant **and** `admission_reserve.local_capacity_verdict(...)` is **not** `too_large`. `prefer-local` / `remote-ok` / absent → `False`; `too_large` → `False` (the request must fall through, never be refused).
  - `_build_local_only_refusal_for_remote()` (~:6686) — replace the raw `preference != _PREF_LOCAL_ONLY` comparison with the predicate, at **both** call sites (`_proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle` ~:10057, `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle` ~:10742). Docstring reworded from "local-only choke point" to "pin-local choke point" naming `local-preferred` (the alias is already normalised upstream, so one branch covers both wire values).
  - The admission-refusal comparison in `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot()` (~:7130, `return ("refused_local_only", ...)`) uses the predicate, so a deferrable `local-preferred` request returns the existing refusal instead of `admission_reject` fall-through, while a `too_large` request keeps the `admission_reject` fall-through with **no** 429.
  - The remote-fallback / direct-guard comparison in the `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle` free-slot path (~:11460 region, `eta_exceeds_budget_direct`) is audited and routed through the same predicate — no third hand-rolled comparison.
  - No new refusal construction: the refusal keeps coming from `_build_local_only_refusal_response()` / `_refusal_retry_timing()` unchanged (the body `verdict` field arrives with LP-0MVSL7SDV007XVG6).
- `proxy/tests/test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` — extend `_EXIT_ROWS` coverage with a `local-preferred` parameterisation. Every row asserts its **own** outcome (no shared assertion):
  - deferrable-classified rows (`thrash_cooldown`, `router_skip_economic`, `router_skip_residency`, `router_skip_tenancy`, `queue_depth_cap`, `queue_wait_expiry`, `admission_guard_free_slot`, `quota_hard_stop`, `chain_cooldown`, `no_local_route`) → `calls == []`, 429, `X-Local-Route: refused`, header reason token and body `reason` agreeing;
  - too-large-classified rows (`router_skip_physical_cap` `context_too_large`, `entry_context_cap`) → `calls == ["remote"]`, 200, no refusal code (parent AC4 boundary; see AC4);
  - **post-dispatch exits** (parent AC1's "slot exhaustion, stall, empty response, sibling-failure"): new rows whose local dispatch *is* attempted once and then fails — slot exhaustion (`slot_info` / 409 lease-active), lease denial after the lease wait (`_lease_action == "fallback"` / `"refused_local_only"`), GPU OOM, `model_loading`, local error status, empty local response (`_is_empty_response`), stall-after-content and sibling/domain failure — each asserting `calls.count("local") == 1`, no `"remote"` in `calls`, 429 with `X-Local-Route: refused` and the recorded reason token. These exits `continue` to the loop head where the choke point decides, so the row proves the structural guarantee rather than assuming it.
- `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py` — a free-slot case: `local-preferred` + free local slot + admitting guard → served locally, no refusal (parent AC2).
- Comments/docstrings at every touched comparison site.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 (parent AC1) With `local-preferred` and a deferrable verdict on each listed exit path, no remote dispatch occurs (asserted per path in tests): pre-dispatch matrix rows assert `calls == []` and post-dispatch local-failure rows assert one local attempt only; every refusal is 429 with `X-Local-Route: refused` and its stable reason token (header and body agreeing), asserted per row with the row's own failure message.
- AC2 (parent AC2) With `local-preferred`, a free local slot and an admitting guard, the request is served locally: `calls == ["local"]`, 200, `X-Local-Route: local`, no 429.
- AC3 The pin decision has exactly one implementation: a test asserts both `_build_local_only_refusal_for_remote` call sites and the admission-refusal path consult the same predicate, and that the predicate reads the canonical `admission_reserve` constants and `local_capacity_verdict()` (a spy/patch proves the helper is the only verdict source — no `if reason in (...)` table in `provider.py`).
- AC4 A `too_large` request is **never** refused by this path: the two size rows dispatch remote with `calls == ["remote"]` and 200, and no local-capacity 429 body is produced. (Chain-level stripping and the promoted log line belong to LP child "too-large promotion"; this AC pins only "no refusal".)
- AC5 (parent AC5) Requires no change to response shape for `prefer-local` / `remote-ok` / remote-less chains: the existing matrix rows pass **unmodified**, and every anchored response keeps its headers/body apart from the additive `verdict` field delivered by LP-0MVSL7SDV007XVG6.

- AC7 (parent AC7) Comments and docstrings updated at every touched comparison site and in the refusal builder; operator-facing docs (`proxy/docs/`, `proxy/config.yaml` commentary) remain out of scope — tracked in LP-0MVSHXU8E004BL57.
- AC8 (parent AC8) Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (the changed-scope gate `/skill:test --scope changed` first; the full suite is enforced by the dev-push gate).

## Constraints

- **Never promote a fits-local request.** A `deferrable` request that cannot run now is refused/deferred, never silently moved to a paid provider (parent assumption A2).
- **Never refuse a too-large request** for local capacity; it falls through (parent AC4). Do not implement chain stripping here.
- **Single preference source:** compare against `admission_reserve.PREF_LOCAL_PREFERRED` (and the verdict constants); no `"local-only"` / `"local-preferred"` literal comparison in `provider.py` (LP-0MVSHWYVE005MS16 AC4 stays enforced).
- **Single verdict source:** `admission_reserve.local_capacity_verdict()`; no re-derived classification.
- **Untouched:** `_refusal_retry_timing()`, queue bounds (`contention_queue_max_wait_seconds`, `contention_queue_max_depth`), config defaults, response field names.
- **Fail-safe direction:** an unclassifiable exit stays pinned (helper returns `deferrable`), so an unknown reason can never promote to remote.
- Scope guard: no queue UX work (LP-0MVIKPRMD000Y97R), no client-side herdr/pi work.

# Feature: deferral — queue-budget expiry yields a retryable 429

Parent: LP-0MVSHXTLS000VMLE. Depends on: LP child "local-preferred pin across every local-route exit" (the pin predicate and the refusal path).

## Goal

A `local-preferred` request the verdict classifies `deferrable` waits in the existing contention queue, and when that wait budget (or the queue depth cap) is exhausted it gets a **retryable** 429 built by the truthful-timing helper — not a remote dispatch and not "All providers exhausted". The request is enqueued at most once, no lease or queue slot leaks, and the response is stamped once.

## Deliverables

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` (`_proxy_with_fallback_cycle`, local dispatch gate ~:10824-:10905, the lease-active fallback ~:10713-:10756, and the lease path ~:11933):
  - Both contention-queue exits — `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue` (wait budget expired) and the depth-cap exit (never enqueued) — are converted, for a pin-local + `deferrable` request, into a single refusal produced by `_build_local_only_refusal_response()` instead of falling through to the next provider.
  - The refusal reason is the existing canonical queue token `fallback_after_queue` (recorded through `_note_local_fallback_reason()` so the header and body agree); the timing stays entirely inside `_refusal_retry_timing()`, fed with the measured wait through `advertised_retry_after` (the queue's measured/remaining budget) so `Retry-After` / `retry_at` reflect the real wait rather than a re-derived estimate.
  - The refusal is returned **before** any remote candidate is resolved/dispatched and before any attempt/cooldown/usage-limit state is written, so nothing is enqueued twice and no lease is taken for a request that is being refused.
  - The lease-active fallback loop (~:10713, which currently walks to the next remote provider) must not run for a pin-local `deferrable` request; its refusal names `local_lease_active`.
- `proxy/tests/test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` — pin the two queue rows for `local-preferred` with explicit field assertions (`queue_wait_expiry`, `queue_depth_cap`).
- `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py` (or a focused addition) — queue-invariant assertions: enqueue-once, queue depth restored, no lease leak, single header stamp.
- Docstrings/comments on the converted branches: state that deferral ends in a retryable refusal and why (a fits-local request must never be promoted).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 (parent AC3) With `local-preferred` and a deferrable verdict after the queue budget, the response is 429 with `retryable: true`, a `Retry-After`/`retry_at` pair consistent with the refusal timing contract (`retry_at` ≈ now + `Retry-After` within a small tolerance), `X-Local-Route: refused`, and a body verdict of `deferrable`; body `reason == "fallback_after_queue"` equals the `X-Local-Fallback-Reason` header.
- AC2 (parent AC3) The depth-cap exit (queue full, request never enqueued) produces the same retryable 429 shape and leaves the held waiter untouched (`contention_queue.queue_depth()` unchanged, 0 leaked).
- AC3 (parent AC1) With `local-preferred` and a deferrable verdict on each queue exit path, no remote dispatch occurs (asserted per path in tests): `calls == []` for both rows, and the response is not an exhaustion response (no `EXHAUSTION_*` code, no "All providers exhausted" text).
- AC4 (parent AC6) No queue-depth, lease or slot leak and no double header stamping on any of the above (asserted in tests): the request is enqueued at most once, `contention_queue.queue_depth()` returns to its pre-request value after the refusal, no local lease remains registered for the session, and `X-Local-Route` is stamped once — asserted on both queue exits and on the lease-active fallback.
- AC5 (parent AC6) Single stamping: the refusal is not re-stamped by the top-level `_stamp_local_route_headers()` (a patched stamp helper is never invoked with an already-stamped refusal).
- AC6 Truthful timing is preserved by construction: a test asserts the refusal's timing equals `_refusal_retry_timing("fallback_after_queue", advertised_retry_after=<measured remainder>)`, and the over-budget reasons still carry **no** `Retry-After` (existing `test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` / `test_local_admission_guard.py` rows stay green unmodified).
- AC7 (parent AC5) Requires no change to response shape for `prefer-local` / `remote-ok` / remote-less chains: they still fall through to the next provider after queue expiry exactly as today, and a remote-less (`private`) chain still defers and never promotes (parent assumption A5).
- AC8 (parent AC7) Comments and docstrings updated at every converted branch; operator-facing docs remain out of scope (LP-0MVSHXU8E004BL57).
- AC9 (parent AC8) Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (changed-scope gate first; the full suite is enforced by the dev-push gate).

## Constraints

- **Queue bounds unchanged:** `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` (60 s) and `contention_queue_max_depth` keep their current values; no new config key or default.
- **No new queue implementation:** reuse `proxy/contention_queue.py` exactly as is (no priority promotion, no lease-grace tuning — that is LP-0MVIKPRMD000Y97R).
- **No timer renegotiation:** `_refusal_retry_timing()` owns `Retry-After` / `retry_at`; this slice only supplies an already-measured remainder through `advertised_retry_after`.
- **No promotion of a fits-local request** and no deferral of a too-large one (the latter is already stripped by LP child "too-large promotion").
- **Exactly one enqueue and one stamp**; a refusal must not leave attempt/cooldown state behind.
- No double refusal: the pin path (LP child C1) and this deferral path must not both build a response for the same request.

## Existing state (verified during planning)

- `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot()` (`proxy/proxy/provider.py` ~:7087-:7200) returns `("fallback", None, elapsed)` when `contention_queue.wait_for_local_slot()` returns `None` (caps exceeded), `("dispatch", None, elapsed)` when a slot frees, `("context_bypass", ...)` for size skips and `("refused_local_only", ...)` for the admission refusal. It stamps `request._local_queue_saturation` and `request._contention_queue_wait_seconds`.
- `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle` handles the gate result around :10824-:10905: `contention_queue_dispatch` (queued and dispatched) and `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue` (queued, budget expired → falls through to the next provider). The lease-active branch (~:10899) walks to the next remote provider.
- `contention_queue.wait_for_local_slot(max_wait_seconds, max_depth, slot_free_check, session_id, retained, eta_seconds, eta_ordering, promote_after_seconds)` returns `None` on cap exhaustion; `contention_queue.queue_depth()` exposes the current waiter count (used by existing tests).
- `_refusal_retry_timing(reason, eta_prefill_seconds=..., budget_seconds=..., projected_wait_seconds=..., advertised_retry_after=..., config=...)` (:4483) — `prefill_budget_exceeded` / `context_too_large` are in `NOT_TIME_RETRYABLE_REFUSAL_REASONS` (:4440); any other reason (including `fallback_after_queue`) keeps an ETA-derived timer with a 1 s floor and the `max_retry_after_seconds` cap, and honours `advertised_retry_after`.
- `_build_local_only_refusal_response(attempt, config)` (:~6530) builds the 429 from the attempt dict (`reason`, `eta_prefill_seconds`, `budget_seconds`, `projected_wait_seconds`) and stamps `X-Local-Route: refused`.
- Existing tests already cover the queue rows for `local-only` and `prefer-local`: `test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py::_EXIT_ROWS` rows `queue_depth_cap` and `queue_wait_expiry`, with `_occupy_the_only_queue_slot()` seeding the depth cap and `contention_queue.reset()` in the autouse fixture.

## Key Files:

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — queue-exit conversion in `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle`, lease-active fallback, `_build_local_only_refusal_response()` call, `_note_local_fallback_reason()` for `fallback_after_queue`.
- `proxy/proxy/contention_queue.py` — consumed only (`wait_for_local_slot()`, `queue_depth()`, `reset()`); no change.
- `proxy/tests/test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` — per-row retryable-429 assertions for the two queue exits.
- `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py` — enqueue-once / no-leak / single-stamp invariants.

## Dependency graph (wired 2026-10-28)

- Depends on: LP-0MVSLZY470051ZB2 (local-preferred pin across every local-route exit).
- Depended on by: LP-0MVSM06Z8003UQTM (routing-outcome line).
- The too-large strip (LP-0MVSM06LB001PRU4) is a sibling and does not overlap: that child removes the local entry before the queue is ever entered.

# Feature: too-large promotion — local stripped from the effective chain

Parent: LP-0MVSHXTLS000VMLE. Depends on: LP child "local-preferred pin across every local-route exit" (pin predicate, verdict plumbing in both cycles).

## Goal

When the capacity verdict is `too_large`, the local route is not attempted at all: the local entry is removed from the effective chain at resolution time (the same structural filter `remote-ok` already uses), so the remote tiers serve the request with no local attempt, no queueing, no deferral and no local-capacity 429. A remote-less chain (e.g. `private`) is never stripped — it keeps deferring and never promotes (parent assumption A5).

## Deliverables

- `proxy/proxy/priority.py`:
  - Extend the chain filter so a `too_large` verdict removes every `type: local` entry — reuse the **existing** `remote-ok` comprehension rather than adding a second filter, e.g. `apply_local_preference(chain, preference, verdict=None)` treating `CAPACITY_TOO_LARGE` as "strip local". No new preference literal, no second chain-filter implementation.
  - Docstring states the two stripping reasons (`remote-ok` by preference, `too_large` by capacity) and the remote-less-chain carve-out.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` (both cycles, `_proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle` ~:9991 and `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle` ~:10664):
  - Compute the capacity verdict **once per request** before the dispatch loop, from the already-built `_RoutingEstimateCache` plus `server.local_cold_prefill_budget_tokens` (via `prefill_eta.COLD_PREFILL_BUDGET_KEY`) and the local entry's context ceiling, through `admission_reserve.local_capacity_verdict(...)`; cache it on the request (e.g. `request._local_capacity_verdict`) so the refusal builder and the observability slice reuse it instead of recomputing.
  - Apply the verdict-aware filter to the cycle's chain before the `while True:` loop, so the local entry is never resolved, never queued and never refused. Guard the call so a chain with **no** non-local entry is left intact (empty-chain exhaustion must never be produced by stripping).
  - Stamp the outcome for the observability slice (`request._local_routing_outcome = "promoted"` / a shared constant), no separate log line here.
- Tests:
  - `proxy/tests/test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` — a `local-preferred` + `too_large` row set: `calls == ["remote"]`, 200, no refusal code, `contention_queue.queue_depth() == 0`, and (with free local slots) the local dispatch stub never invoked.
  - `proxy/tests/test_priority_routing.py` — unit tests for the verdict-aware filter (strip on `too_large`, keep on `deferrable`, identical shape to `remote-ok`, remote-less chain untouched).
- Comments/docstrings at the filter and both cycle call sites.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 (parent AC4) With `local-preferred` and a `too_large` verdict, the chain excludes local and a remote provider serves the request; no 429 is produced for local capacity (the local dispatch is never attempted, `calls == ["remote"]`, 200, nothing queued).
- AC2 The verdict is computed once per request before the dispatch loop and reused: a spy on `admission_reserve.local_capacity_verdict()` asserts one call per request per cycle and that the value is cached on the request for the refusal/observability paths.
- AC3 (parent A5, parent AC5) A remote-less chain (every entry `type: local`, e.g. `private`) is never stripped even when the verdict is `too_large`: the local route is still attempted and the existing deferral/refusal behaviour applies; no empty-chain "All providers exhausted" is produced by the filter.
- AC4 No second chain-filter implementation: a unit test asserts the verdict-stripped chain is identical to the `remote-ok`-stripped chain for the same input, and that `provider.py` introduces no new `type == "local"` filtering loop nor a new preference literal.
- AC5 (parent AC5) Requires no change to response shape for `prefer-local` / `remote-ok` / remote-less chains, including when the verdict is `too_large` (existing `test_priority_routing.py` and matrix rows pass unmodified).
- AC6 (parent AC6) No queue-depth, lease or slot leak and no double header stamping on any of the above (asserted in tests): the promoted path engages no queue or lease (`contention_queue.queue_depth() == 0`, no lease registered), the request is dispatched exactly once, and one `X-Local-Route` header is stamped.
- AC7 (parent AC7) Comments and docstrings updated (filter + both cycle call sites); operator-facing docs remain out of scope (LP-0MVSHXU8E004BL57).
- AC8 (parent AC8) Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (changed-scope gate first; the full suite is enforced by the dev-push gate).

## Constraints

- **Never promote a fits-local request:** only the `too_large` verdict strips local (parent assumption A2). Unclassifiable verdicts are `deferrable` (helper fail-safe) and stay pinned.
- **Never defer a too-large request:** stripping happens before the dispatch loop, i.e. before any queue entry.
- **Reuse, don't rebuild:** the existing `remote-ok` filter, `prefill_eta.COLD_PREFILL_BUDGET_KEY`, the existing routing estimate cache; no new estimator, no new sizing model (parent assumption A1).
- **Config defaults unchanged**, queue bounds unchanged.
- **No log line here** — the single per-request outcome line is LP child "routing-outcome line"; this slice only stamps the outcome.
- Scope guard: no `cached_ratio`/economic-bypass policy change, no contention-queue work (LP-0MVIKPRMD000Y97R).

## Existing state (verified during planning)

- `proxy/proxy/priority.py:410` `apply_local_preference(chain, preference)` — strips `type: local` entries only when `preference == "remote-ok"` (literal comparison removed by LP-0MVSHWVE005MS16); `:431` `effective_chain_for_request(request, model_config, server_config)` calls it. Both cycles call `effective_chain_for_request()` *before* the body has been read, which is why the verdict-aware strip cannot live inside the preference filter alone and must be applied by the cycle once the routing estimate exists.
- `_proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle` (`provider.py:9901`): chain resolution at :9991, `_raw_body = await request.body()` / `_routing_estimate = _RoutingEstimateCache(...)` at ~:10030-:10048, then `while True:` at ~:10053.
- `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle` (`provider.py:10572`): chain resolution at :10664, `body_json` and `_routing_estimate` built at ~:10640-:10700, then `while True:` at ~:10700.
- `_RoutingEstimateCache` (`provider.py`, used at both cycles) computes the authoritative routing estimate once per cycle — the input the verdict needs; `_provider_context_limit(provider_cfg)` (:3235) exposes the per-entry context ceiling (`max_context_tokens`), and `server.local_model_ctx_size` is the global local context cap.
- `prefill_eta.COLD_PREFILL_BUDGET_KEY = "local_cold_prefill_budget_tokens"` (`prefill_eta.py:209`); the shipped default is 25 000 (parent assumption A1).
- `admission_reserve.local_capacity_verdict(...)` (delivered by LP-0MVSL7QJW006OYPB) classifies `new_tokens > budget_tokens`, `prefill_budget_exceeded` and `context_too_large` as `too_large`; everything else, including unknown tokens, as `deferrable`.
- `proxy/tests/test_priority_routing.py` (~430 lines) already tests `effective_chain_for_request()`; `test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` rows `router_skip_physical_cap` (`context_too_large`) and `entry_context_cap` are the natural `too_large` fixtures.

## Key Files:

- `proxy/proxy/priority.py` — verdict-aware chain filter reusing the `remote-ok` strip, docstring.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — pre-loop verdict computation and chain strip in both cycles, verdict caching on the request, outcome stamp.
- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py` — consumed only: `CAPACITY_TOO_LARGE`, `local_capacity_verdict()`.
- `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py` — consumed only: `COLD_PREFILL_BUDGET_KEY`.
- `proxy/tests/test_priority_routing.py` — filter unit tests (strip/keep/remote-less/`remote-ok` parity).
- `proxy/tests/test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` — end-to-end promoted-row assertions (remote only, no 429, no queue).

## Dependency graph (wired 2026-10-28)

- Depends on: LP-0MVSLZY470051ZB2 (local-preferred pin across every local-route exit).
- Depended on by: LP-0MVSM06Z8003UQTM (routing-outcome line).
- Sibling of record: LP-0MVSM06BK008FZUE (deferral) — that child handles the `deferrable` queue expiry; this child guarantees a `too_large` request never reaches it.
